contract.settlement_definition: Live series (7, all with rules text): player count props KXNFLTD ('scores at least 1+ touchdowns', floor_strike 0.5 'greater'), KXNFLANYTD ('scores a touchdown'), KXNFL2TD ('scores two or more touchdowns'), KXNFLTDPROT (protected N+, e.g. floor 1.5 '2+'); ordinal scorer props KXNFLFIRSTTD (scores the first touchdown of the game), KXNFLTEAMFIRSTTD (scores the first touchdown for his team) and KXNFLNEXTTD (scores the k-th touchdown of the game, e.g. '4th TD'). YES when the named player is credited with the required touchdown(s) in the game. Active-but-no-snap players settle to the (last) fair market price before game start; once he takes one snap, even one nullified by penalty, the market settles on touchdowns scored. Ordinal markets carry a 'No Touchdown (Scorer)' strike that resolves YES, with all player strikes NO, if no (team / k-th) touchdown is scored. Protected contracts settle at the pre-kickoff fair price if the player plays in the first half but in no play after it (including overtime) unless he already reached the count. KXNFLTD/FIRSTTD state fake-punt/fake-FG TDs by the offence are not special-teams TDs. No sampled text states whether overtime touchdowns count for the count or ordinal props; source of truth is the official game result/scoring summary.

rules_evidence.quote: If DJ Moore is active but never takes a snap, the market settles to the fair market price before game start.
rules_evidence.establishes: Zero-snap active players are voided to a fair price, not lost; the pregame-priced probability is conditional on taking a snap.

rules_evidence.quote: If no Buffalo touchdowns are scored in the game, the No Buffalo Touchdown market resolves to Yes and all other player markets resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: The team-first contract is conditional on the team scoring at all; a no-team-TD strike absorbs the zero case.

rules_evidence.establishes: Protected N+ contracts carry a half-time exit void rule that truncates the injury-exit tail.

rules_evidence.quote: Touchdowns scored on fake punts or field goals by the offensive team do not count as a special teams touchdown.
rules_evidence.establishes: Trick-play scores are attributed to the offence/the scoring player, so a skill player's fake-punt TD counts for him.

rules_evidence.quote: If Connor Heyward scores the first touchdown in Las Vegas vs San Francisco Pro Football game
rules_evidence.establishes: The game-first scorer contract is the first TD of the whole game by either team, i.e. a cross-team race followed by scorer allocation.

rules_evidence.establishes: KXNFLNEXTTD is an ordinal contract on the k-th touchdown of the game (here the 4th), not a next-from-now contract.

rules_evidence.establishes: The k-th TD contract has a no-k-th-TD strike, so P(game TD count >= k) enters directly.

rules_evidence.quote: Once a player takes at least one snap, even if nullified by penalty, the market settles based on touchdowns scored.
rules_evidence.establishes: The 2+ series uses the same one-snap participation gate as the anytime series.

rules_evidence.quote: If no touchdowns are scored in the game, the No Touchdown Scorer market resolves to Yes and all other player markets resolve to No.

variants_and_edge_cases: Families: (a) player N+ count props (KXNFLTD, ANYTD, 2TD, TDPROT); (b) ordinal scorer props: game-first (FIRSTTD), team-first (TEAMFIRSTTD) and k-th TD of the game (NEXTTD, listed per ordinal e.g. 'TD4'). Team TD counts (KXNFLTEAMTD) and D/ST TD (KXNFLDSTTD) were re-filed to game_events and are no longer claimed here.

KXNFLNEXTTD is the k-th touchdown of the game counted from kickoff; P(YES) = P(game TDs >= k) x P(player scores the k-th | it occurs). The sampled NEXTTD ticker and text date the Seattle-New England game Feb 6, 2026 while the ANYTD and 2TD samples date the same matchup Feb 8 (a date discrepancy, not explained); the market is closed, so listing time (pregame vs in-game after earlier TDs) is not visible.

Zero-snap void: non-protected props use 'fair market price before game start' (KXNFLTEAMFIRSTTD, KXNFLFIRSTTD, KXNFLTD) or 'last fair market price before game start' (KXNFLANYTD, 2TD, NEXTTD); the effective event is TD | at least one snap.
Protected contracts (KXNFLTDPROT) pay fair price on a first-half-only participant unless the count was already reached; strike floor 1.5 with 'greater', i.e. integer N+ with no push.

No sampled text addresses overtime touchdowns, defensive/return touchdowns by a named offensive player's team in team-first markets, laterals or stat corrections; these are recorded as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.

mechanism.summary: A player's first-TD or anytime-TD outcome is the product of five stochastic layers. (1) He must take a snap (and, for protected props, play after halftime) or the contract voids. (2) His team must score touchdowns rather than field goals: a Poisson-binomial count over roughly 10-12 drives, with TD vs FG decided by red-zone and 4th-and-goal policy. (3) Each TD is allocated to a scorer through a categorical draw over rushers, receivers, the QB and non-offensive units, where the weights depend on field position at the TD (a 1-yard plunge versus a 40-yard throw), the personnel package and the game script. (4) For first-TD markets the two teams race: the first TD goes to the team whose drive converts first, so opening possession, scripted opening drives and defensive/special-teams scores determine team order, and then that team's first-TD scorer distribution (different from its average TD scorer distribution) applies. (5) For 2+ TD contracts, within-player TD counts are overdispersed relative to Poisson because goal-line role and a high-scoring game state are shared across a player's TDs. The pool, allocation and ordering layers must be modelled separately; a single 'TD rate' conflates them.

stages.name: Participation gate and void states
stages.description: The contract only pays or loses if the player takes a snap; active-but-no-snap voids to a pregame fair price and a protected contract voids on a first-half-only appearance. So the modelled quantity is P(TD | plays), plus a separate P(void) that affects sizing but not the label. Drivers are the Friday designation, the 90-minute inactive list, depth-chart role (a gadget RB3 may be active and never see a snap), and in-game injury exit hazard by position and snap load. Early exits shorten the exposure window; late exits matter less once the TD is already recorded for protected markets.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli at status level (active/inactive), then a position-specific hazard of leaving the game; protected void adds a halftime step function; discrete and heavily mass-at-0/1 near kickoff

stages.name: Team TD pool and TD-versus-FG conversion
stages.description: The team's expected touchdown count is drives times P(TD per drive). The value that matters for scorer markets is touchdowns, not points: an implied total of 24 can be 3 TDs and a FG or 2 TDs and 3 FGs. Red-zone TD rate, 4th-and-goal go-for-it policy, kicker range and opponent red-zone defense decide the split. The team TD mean is derived from the model (drives times TD-per-drive, nfl.model_team_td_mean) and regressed because red-zone TD rate has low year-to-year stability; market-implied team totals are used only as a benchmark, never as an input.
stages.distribution: Count of 1 to 5 TDs per team per game; approx Poisson-binomial with mild overdispersion from game-state sharing; discrete, right-skewed

stages.name: TD source and scorer allocation within the team
stages.description: Each team TD is drawn from a categorical distribution over rushers (including QB sneaks and scrambles), receivers by route and target role, and unit-level scores (pick-six, return). The weights are not season TD shares: they are a function of the yard line at which the score occurs, which is a function of the drive type. Goal-line carries inside the 3 and end-zone targets behave very differently from open-field touches. Teammate absences shift weights non-proportionally because a replacement has a different goal-line role than the player he replaces. Realized TD counts regress heavily to opportunity-based expectation.
stages.distribution: Categorical with player-specific weights; TD per carry convex in distance to the goal line; high noise at player level because a player sees only 3-10 goal-line touches per season-quarter

stages.name: Ordinal TD allocation: team-first, game-first and k-th touchdown
stages.description: Three ordinal contracts differ. KXNFLTEAMFIRSTTD: P = P(team scores >=1 TD) x P(player scores the team's first TD | team scores); opponent and opening possession matter little and a 'No <team> Touchdown' strike absorbs the zero case. KXNFLFIRSTTD adds a competing-risk race for the game's first TD: opening possession, each side's per-drive TD probability on drives 1-3 (nfl.drive_outcome_by_index) and defensive/return TDs decide which team scores first, then that team's first-TD scorer distribution applies. KXNFLNEXTTD settles on the k-th TD of the game: P = P(game TD count >= k) x a scorer share for the k-th TD that drifts with script (a trailing team's passing share rises later), so it needs the joint game TD-count distribution from both teams' pools rather than a single team-first share.
stages.distribution: Competing-risk process over alternating drives with geometric-like per-drive first-TD hazard; for the k-th TD a count-threshold probability P(N_game>=k) times a categorical scorer share that shifts with score state

stages.name: Multiplicity and cross-TD dependence
stages.description: 2+ TD (protected) contracts and anytime markets need P(N>=k) for a player, not just P(N>=1). A player's TDs are positively dependent: a high team total and his goal-line role both scale every TD, and an early TD signals a favourable script. The count is therefore a mixed Poisson (overdispersed) with a team-level and a role-level shared factor, and team scoring is positively correlated with opponent scoring through pace. The lead-state weights used with nfl.script come from the market-free margin lattice (nfl.model_margin_lattice), not from a spread-implied margin distribution.
stages.distribution: Mixed Poisson / negative-binomial player counts; thick right tail for goal-line backs and WR1s in high-total games

stages.name: Settlement attribution, stat correction and void mechanics
stages.description: Contracts settle on the official scoring summary: who gets credit on fumble-recovery TDs, laterals, nullified plays and kick-return TDs, whether OT TDs count, and the fair-price rule for no-snap or protected exits. Stat corrections can flip a close attribution. The tradable edge also depends on the exact void rule because P(void) changes capital at risk.
stages.distribution: Deterministic rule application given the scoring summary; small probability of post-game stat correction and of ambiguous credit

nfl.player_xtd.label: Player expected touchdowns (xTD) from play-level opportunity
nfl.player_xtd.mechanism: Each rushing attempt and target carries a modelled TD probability that depends on yard line, down and distance, and play type; summing gives an opportunity-based TD expectation independent of luck.
nfl.player_xtd.rationale: Season TD counts and TD rates are dominated by finishing luck (a back with 6 carries inside the 5 can score 0-6). xTD collapses to the opportunity and removes the single-season noise that makes nfl.td_rates misleading.
nfl.player_xtd.measurement: For each rush attempt or target in the player's last 17 team games (half-life 6 games), assign P(TD | yardline_100, down, ydstogo, play_type, is_target) from a league-wide model fit on 2006+ pbp; sum by player; divide by team xTD to get a share. Shrink share to positional prior with k=4 team games' worth of goal-line touches. As-of: through the previous game; recompute after inactives.

nfl.goal_line_personnel.label: Goal-line package and personnel tree (inside the 5)
nfl.goal_line_personnel.mechanism: In goal-to-go snaps inside about the 5-yard line, teams switch to heavy sets (extra TE/OL, FB) and select specific ball carriers and a QB-sneak option, so the TD-eligible set differs from the field-wide rotation.
nfl.goal_line_personnel.rationale: A back who plays 70% of snaps may have zero goal-line role; a 250-pound change-of-pace back may play 5% of snaps and take 60% of inside-the-3 carries. The share of snaps and the share of goal-line carries are different quantities.
nfl.goal_line_personnel.measurement: For snaps with yardline_100 <= 5 over the last 20 team games (half-life 8 games): tabulate by player share of carries, targets, QB sneaks, and offense_personnel (e.g. 22, 23, 12). Report share_carry_i5, share_tgt_i5, sneak_rate and TE/FB TD share. Shrink to team-level rates at k=8 snaps. Zero-fill and flag players who joined the team during the window.

nfl.fourth_and_goal_policy.label: 4th-and-goal and goal-to-go go-for-it policy
nfl.fourth_and_goal_policy.mechanism: On 4th-and-goal from inside the 2-3 yards, coaches either kick a FG or go for the TD, changing the number of TDs and the target and carry mix on those snaps.
nfl.fourth_and_goal_policy.rationale: TD pool is what matters, not points; two teams with equal implied totals can differ by half a TD per game because of this choice. It also drives who receives the final-yard touches.
nfl.fourth_and_goal_policy.measurement: Go-for-it rate on 4th-and-goal with ydstogo <= 3 over the last 2 seasons, opponent and win-probability adjusted: logistic regression on wp, ydstogo, score_differential, time; coach-level random effect with k=12 attempts shrinkage; as-of last game of the prior week; flagged on coach change.
raw_data: pbp: down, ydstogo, yardline_100, wp, play_type
nfl.fourth_and_goal_policy.why: Turns a points forecast into a TD forecast and decides which role gets the last-yard touch.

nfl.team_first_td_attribution.label: Team first-TD scorer attribution history
nfl.team_first_td_attribution.mechanism: The scorer of a team's first TD is drawn from a distribution that differs from the full-game distribution because the first score arises in scripted and early-down contexts.
nfl.team_first_td_attribution.rationale: Scorer shares in first TDs are rated off about 17 events per team-season, so they need strong shrinkage to the full-game xTD share; naive 'first TD hit rate' is nearly pure noise.
nfl.team_first_td_attribution.measurement: For each team-game, record the scorer of the team's first TD and the yard line; compute recency-weighted shares (half-life 20 team games, includes prior-season games at 0.5 weight) and shrink to the player's full-game xTD share with k=10 team first-TD events; output: scorer share and expected yardline.
raw_data: pbp: game_id, posteam, touchdown, td_player_id, yardline_100, drive number
nfl.team_first_td_attribution.why: First-TD props are conditional on the team scoring first, and who scores first differs from who scores overall.

nfl.dst_td_hazard.label: Defensive and special-teams TD hazard per team-game
nfl.dst_td_hazard.mechanism: Pick-sixes, fumble returns, punt and kick return TDs happen at low frequency and are partly attributable to scheme and returner skill but largely random.
nfl.dst_td_hazard.rationale: These events end the 'first TD' contest for every offensive player and count in the team first-TD and D/ST TD markets; they are about 1 in 8-10 team games.
nfl.dst_td_hazard.measurement: Per team-game rate = 0.5*(own takeaway-return TD rate regressed to league mean with k=40 team games + opponent giveaway rate) + returner threat (kick and punt return TD per return, k=60 returns) + opponent special teams allowed rate. Poisson mean; as-of previous game.
raw_data: pbp: interception_return_td flags, fumble_recovery_return_td, returner id
nfl.dst_td_hazard.why: Both first-TD and D/ST TD contracts need an event rate that offensive models ignore.

nfl.zero_snap_active_risk.label: Active-but-zero-snap and protected-void probability
nfl.zero_snap_active_risk.mechanism: A player can be active and take no snap (RB3, TE3, gadget WR), which voids the contract, and protected contracts void on first-half-only exposure.
nfl.zero_snap_active_risk.rationale: The contract is conditional on a snap; ignoring this overstates a low-usage player's effective price and misses the void probability that determines how much capital is truly at risk.
nfl.zero_snap_active_risk.measurement: P(no snap | active) = fraction of last 12 active games with zero offensive snaps, shrunk with a beta prior by depth-chart slot (k=6); P(first-half-only) = fraction of active games with snaps in 1H and none in 2H, plus a Friday-designation uplift from past data; as-of 90-minute inactive list.

inactives by game
nfl.zero_snap_active_risk.why: Directly parameterizes the fair-price void in KXNFLTEAMFIRSTTD and KXNFLTDPROT.

nfl.multi_td_dispersion.label: Within-player multi-TD dispersion factor
nfl.multi_td_dispersion.mechanism: A player's TDs share a latent intensity (team total and goal-line role), so P(2+) exceeds the Poisson implied by P(1+).
nfl.multi_td_dispersion.rationale: 2+ TD contracts and 'multiple touchdowns' markets are priced off the same marginal intensity; dispersion decides the tail ratio P(2+)/P(1+).
nfl.multi_td_dispersion.measurement: Fit a negative-binomial dispersion r by position group (RB goal-line, WR1, TE, QB rush) on the last 5 seasons of player-games with at least 4 expected TD-opportunity touches; report r and P(2+|P(1+)) lookup table; as-of start of week.

nfl.model_team_td_mean.label: Market-free team touchdown mean (drives times TD-per-drive, with FG-vs-TD split)
nfl.model_team_td_mean.mechanism: A team's expected touchdowns are expected drives times the per-drive probability of ending in a touchdown rather than a field goal or no score, estimated from opponent-adjusted offence and defence and red-zone conversion, with no spread, total or price as a feature.
nfl.model_team_td_mean.rationale: Every scorer market is a share of the team's touchdown pool. A points-based implied team total is market-derived and is not touchdown-specific (24 points can be 3 TD + FG or 2 TD + 3 FG). A model-derived TD mean keeps wind, availability and matchup visible and gives P(team scores at least one TD), the quantity the team-own first-TD contract depends on.
nfl.model_team_td_mean.measurement: lambda_TD(team i vs j) = E[drives_i] x P(TD | drive). E[drives] from both teams' neutral seconds per play and expected plays (2015+ pbp, shrink 50/50 to league at 8 games). P(TD|drive) = logistic ridge on own opponent-adjusted offensive EPA per play (half-life 8 games, prior-season weight 0.3 fading to 0 by week 10), opponent defensive EPA per play, red-zone trips per drive and red-zone TD rate (shrunk k=30 trips), 4th-and-goal go-for-it rate (k=12), wind>15 mph and dome flags, starting-QB indicator. Output mean, variance (overdispersion from tercile residuals) and P(N>=1)=1-exp(-lambda_TD) with a negative-binomial correction. As-of: after the previous game, refreshed at the final injury report. Spreads, totals and prices excluded; used only afterwards as a benchmark.

interactions.mechanism: When a primary goal-line back is out, the vacated carries go mainly to whichever back has the next heaviest inside-5 role, not to the next-highest snap player; the shift is non-proportional and can leave a pass-catching back's TD rate unchanged while a rotational power back doubles.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare TD probability change for each teammate when a goal-line player is inactive vs active, grouped by replacement role (power back vs receiving back vs QB), controlling for team xTD.

interactions.mechanism: Team TDs are expected scoring trips times the TD fraction of those trips; a team with an aggressive 4th-and-goal policy and good red-zone offence converts the same total into more TDs, scaling every scorer's probability, while FG-prone teams do the reverse.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress team TD count on the model TD mean with interaction terms for go-for-it rate and red-zone TD rate; the interaction coefficient reveals the uplift.

interactions.mechanism: For the team-own first-TD contract P(player) = P(team has >=1 TD) x P(player | team's first TD): the first factor is set by the team TD mean (rarely below 0.9), the second by scripted early plays and where the first scoring drive starts. A pass-heavy scripted opener moves the second factor toward the WR/TE group away from the goal-line back, and a high team TD mean saturates the first factor so the allocation factor dominates. Opening possession enters only the game-first contracts.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(player is team's first TD scorer) for teams split by model TD-mean tercile and by opener pass rate; confirm the first factor saturates by checking P(team >=1 TD) against lambda, then compare the allocation factor across scripted-opener types.

interactions.mechanism: In wind or heavy precipitation, red-zone pass rate falls and short-yardage runs rise, so receivers' TD share falls and runners' and the QB's rise; the shift is a regime change above a wind threshold, not a linear drift.
interactions.how_to_test: Split goal-to-go plays by wind bucket (<10, 10-15, >15 mph) and compare pass/run TD shares by team.

interactions.mechanism: A player's second TD is much likelier in games where his team's total is high and the team leads, so P(2+) is not a function of P(1+) alone; the shared game-state factor widens the right tail beyond Poisson.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare empirical P(2+|1+) for goal-line backs across model-TD-mean terciles against a Poisson baseline.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in distance to the goal line
nonlinearities.why: TD probability per carry rises from low single-digit percent at the 10 to roughly half or more at the 1; linear yardage-based role shares badly misprice players whose carries are inside versus outside the 5.

Probability that the team scores any TD (the first factor of the team-own first-TD contract and anytime props) is concave in the TD mean, so raising lambda from 3 to 4 changes little while raising it from 1.5 to 2.5 changes a lot; the player's own lambda is team lambda times his share.
Player-level participation switches from near 1 to near 0 across Out/Doubtful/Questionable/Active, so P(void) is a step function of status rather than a smooth variable.

contract.settlement_definition: Six live series, all with rules text. Same-game pre-packs KXNFLPREPACK and KXNFLPREPACKSGP (e.g. 'New York G wins against New England, ... collectively score under 46.5 points') and the championship player-prop parlay KXNFLCOMBO resolve YES only if every leg occurs ('All outcomes encompassed in a market must occur'; 'All Components must resolve to yes'); KXNFLCOMBO player legs are worded 'records at least N+ ... as a participant in both halves'. Cross-game moneyline parlays KXNFLPREPACK2ML/3ML resolve YES if each named team wins its listed game (2 or 3 games, possibly on different days). KXNFLNBA is a cross-league futures conjunction (named NFL team wins the 2026-27 NFL title AND named NBA team wins the 2026-27 NBA title) resolving NO on the first elimination. Settlement source is each leg's official result. No sampled combo text states how a voided/postponed leg, a push on an integer line, a tie, or overtime is handled, nor what happens to a 'both halves' player leg when the player misses a half.

rules_evidence.quote: All outcomes encompassed in a market must occur for the market to resolve Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Same-game pre-packs are strict conjunctions of their legs; no partial credit, so leg dependence decides the price.

rules_evidence.quote: If New York G wins against New England, New York G and New England collectively score under 46.5 points
rules_evidence.establishes: A two-leg same-game pack of a winner leg and a half-point total leg: winner and total are dependent through the score lattice.

rules_evidence.quote: If New England wins against Denver, Seattle wins against Los Angeles R
rules_evidence.establishes: Cross-game moneyline parlay: each leg is a different game, so the joint is near a product of win probabilities.

rules_evidence.quote: San Francisco wins against Seattle, Denver wins against Buffalo, Los Angeles R wins against Chicago
rules_evidence.establishes: Three-game moneyline parlay spanning two dates (Jan 17 and Jan 18 games).

rules_evidence.quote: If Drake Maye records at least 225+ passing yards as a participant in both halves of the 2026 Pro Football Championship
rules_evidence.establishes: Championship player-prop parlay legs carry a participation-in-both-halves condition on each player leg.

rules_evidence.quote: All Components must resolve to yes for this market to resolve to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The championship combo is a strict conjunction of player-prop components.

rules_evidence.quote: If one of the teams is eliminated from championship contention in the 2026-27 Pro Football and Pro Basketball seasons, then the market resolves to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: The cross-league combo is a two-leg futures conjunction that can resolve NO early on the first elimination.

variants_and_edge_cases: Four variants: (a) same-game packs (PREPACK winner+total, PREPACKSGP), (b) cross-game moneyline parlays (PREPACK2ML, PREPACK3ML) over 2-3 games on possibly different dates, (c) single-game player-prop parlays (KXNFLCOMBO, Super Bowl, 5+ player legs with 'participant in both halves' wording), (d) cross-league futures (KXNFLNBA).
Moneyline legs ('wins against') in regular-season parlays can end in a tie after overtime; no sampled text says whether a tied leg is a loss or a void.

KXNFLCOMBO player legs require the player to be 'a participant in both halves'; the truncated text does not say whether failing that condition makes the leg NO or voids the combo, which matters for injury-exit risk across 5+ players.
Half-point totals (46.5, 41.5) cannot push, but integer lines in other packs could; push handling inside packs is not stated.
KXNFLPREPACKSGP titles are template-mangled ('Over 56.5 points scored wins against ...'), so leg identity must be read from market metadata, not the title.
Cross-league futures combos resolve at different dates (Super Bowl in February, NBA Finals in June) with early NO on elimination; same-game dependence inputs do not apply to them.
contract.settlement_data_source: Per-leg official game results and box scores (NFL game book) for packs and parlays; NFL and NBA official championship results for KXNFLNBA. Leg-void, tie and push handling is not stated in the sampled text.

mechanism.summary: A combo's probability is the probability of an intersection of leg events, so the objects to model are the dependence structure and the joint support, not the marginals. In football all same-game legs are functions of one latent process: the drive sequence. A single drive outcome (a 12-play field-goal drive versus a 2-play deep touchdown) simultaneously moves team points, quarter scoring, the QB's yards and TDs, the rusher's attempts, and the clock that decides how many more drives occur. Hard accounting identities link the legs: individual yards cannot exceed the team total, individual TDs sum to team TDs, a team's points must be 3a+6b+... in discrete steps, and the winner's margin and the game total are tied through team scores. Between games there is near independence, apart from shared weather, referee crew or league-wide shocks. So the pricing task is: (i) good legs, (ii) a joint simulator or copula calibrated to these identities and to regime-dependent dependence (script, QB status, weather), (iii) exact leg wording so that void/push/OT states are handled, and (iv) execution cost and thin liquidity once a price exists.

stages.name: Leg marginals from the underlying archetype models
stages.description: Each leg inherits a marginal probability from the model of its own archetype: spread and moneyline from the margin distribution, total from drive-by-drive scoring, QB yards from attempts and efficiency, TD scorer from the allocation model. If the marginals are wrongly calibrated, the joint is wrong whatever the copula; the combo error is approximately the sum of leg errors because probabilities multiply. Marginals must also be coherent with each other (for example, a team total leg and a game total leg imply an opponent total). The marginals are an explicit dependency on the model outputs of the sibling archetypes (moneyline/spread, total, QB, scorer); this record does not rebuild them and uses market-free team means, never ratings implied by lines. The dependency is now an explicit interface (nfl.sibling_leg_marginal_interface): each sibling archetype exports its leg P(yes) and shared simulation draws of home/away points, margin, total, plays, availability and weather bin, so legs are read from the same draws.
stages.distribution: Each leg is Bernoulli with its own probability; the joint support is a subset of {0,1}^k with k = 2 to 6 legs; errors in marginals compound multiplicatively across legs

stages.name: Shared latent game state
stages.description: Same-game legs depend on the same latent variables: expected margin, expected total, pace, QB and key-player availability, weather and the lead state across time. A trailing script raises the QB's attempts and yards and lowers the favourite's rushing, so favourite-cover and the trailing team's QB yards are negatively related (and the leading team's QB yards positively only while the game is competitive) even though 'good team' and 'high total' are positively related. These dependencies are regime-dependent: the sign of the correlation between a rusher's yardage and the favourite covering flips between competitive and blowout games.
stages.distribution: Continuous latent factors (margin ~ N-ish with key-number lattice, total, pace) driving conditional Bernoulli legs; dependence is conditional and non-constant across regimes

stages.name: Accounting identities and hard constraints
stages.description: Football box-score numbers obey sums: the TDs of all players on a team sum to the team's offensive TDs, individual receiving yards are bounded by the team's passing yards, and team points are non-negative combinations of 7, 3, 2, 6 and 8. These constraints create dependence that Gaussian correlations miss: two teammates both scoring first-TD legs is impossible, and two skill players both going over their yardage lines requires a large passing team total.
stages.distribution: Deterministic constraints on a discrete lattice; produces exactly zero joint probability for incompatible leg sets and large non-Gaussian dependence in the tails

stages.name: Leg wording: push, void, overtime and fair-price states
stages.description: The joint event is determined by each leg's own settlement text. Legs ending in a push on integer lines, voided on postponement, excluding overtime, or settling at a fair price on a no-snap player each remove or alter the event. A combo containing a regulation-only leg and a full-game leg has a joint outcome that diverges whenever the game is tied after 60 minutes. Combo contract text decides if a voided leg is dropped or whether the combo is cancelled. KXNFLCOMBO adds a participation condition ('as a participant in both halves') to each player leg, so an in-game exit by any of the named players can decide the combo regardless of the stat.
stages.distribution: Rule-based, deterministic given leg and combo wording; tiny probability of tie/postponement but concentrated on key numbers

stages.name: Execution cost, fees and book thinness
stages.description: Once a model joint probability exists, realized edge is the model joint minus the executable price, fees (often a larger share of a long-shot combo price) and the cost of hedging legs that do not exist as markets. Combo books are thin and stale, so the price can reflect a market-maker's correlation assumption rather than information. This stage is execution economics, not game information; it is context for trade evaluation and does not count as an input interaction.
stages.distribution: Price is a dealer quote; edge is small relative to spread; deterministic fee schedule applies to the whole combo payoff

stages.name: Cross-league futures conjunction
stages.description: KXNFLNBA pays only if a named NFL team wins the Super Bowl and a named NBA team wins the NBA Finals of the same 2026-27 cycle. The NFL leg is a season-long playoff path (seeding, bye, single-elimination games) produced by a standings and playoff simulation; the NBA leg is a best-of-seven playoff path from that sport's own model. The two are effectively independent, so the price is near the product of the legs, but the NFL leg resolves in February and early elimination of either team resolves NO, so the combo's value path is front-loaded by the NFL season.
stages.distribution: Product of two small, independent Bernoulli probabilities (each typically under 0.2); absorbing early-NO state on the first elimination

stages.name: Cross-game moneyline parlays on one slate or round
stages.description: KXNFLPREPACK2ML/3ML pay if each named team wins its own game, e.g. three divisional-round games on Jan 17-18. Each leg's win probability comes from that game's market-free margin lattice including overtime (regular-season ties possible). Legs are different games, so the dependence is weak and comes only from shared model error (a common rating-system bias applied to all games), shared weather systems or officiating directives, and in playoffs from nothing structural. The joint is therefore close to the product of leg probabilities, and the main error source is miscalibration of each leg compounding multiplicatively; overestimating dependence would misprice favourites-parlays.
stages.distribution: Product of 2-3 Bernoulli legs with p roughly 0.2-0.85 each; small positive residual correlation via shared model error; tie mass per regular-season leg about 0.4%

stages.name: Shared weather state as a common shock across same-game legs
stages.description: At open-air venues a single kickoff weather state moves several legs together: sustained wind above roughly 15 mph or heavy precipitation lowers the game and team totals, cuts kicker points and long-field-goal legs, lowers QB passing-yard and receiver-yard legs and pushes play-calling toward the run, raising the lead back's carries. Same-direction combos (under, QB under, kicker under) therefore have joint probability above the product of marginals and mixed combos below it. Domes and closed roofs remove the shock entirely, and forecast uncertainty at quote time means the joint must integrate over the weather distribution, not plug in a point forecast.
stages.distribution: Regime mixture over calm, moderate and severe weather bins; within a bin legs share mean shifts and a residual correlation; zero effect for roofed games

talent_strength.note: Team strength enters through the market-free team points mean that feeds side and total leg marginals; market-implied ratings are benchmarks only. For the cross-league futures combo, NFL team strength enters through the season simulation.

opponent_matchup.note: Matchup effects live inside each leg's own archetype model and enter the combo only through its marginals; the combo layer adds no separate opponent-matchup variable.

role_personnel.note: Role shares matter through the identity that player outputs sum to team outputs.

availability_news.note: A QB or WR1 scratch moves several legs at once, so availability is a shared factor.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching tendencies act through team marginals and script, which are already represented by the script lattice; no combo-specific coaching variable exists.

environment.note: Shared weather enters the joint draw as a regime variable (calm/moderate/severe) coupling total, kicker, QB/receiver yards and rusher legs; elasticities by leg pair remain to be estimated.

game_context_script.note: Lead-state script is the main source of cross-leg dependence.

pace_volume.note: Plays and drives are shared across volume legs; covered via the correlation matrix.

efficiency_conversion.note: Marginal stat shapes for each leg; conversion luck is in each leg's own model.

distribution_variance.note: Joint distribution on the score lattice with constraints for same-game packs; residual cross-game dependence for multi-game moneyline parlays.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, stakes and motivation affect legs only through each leg's own marginal; they create no separate dependency channel between legs at the combo layer.

nfl.team_stat_accounting_constraints.label: Team-to-player accounting constraints for same-game legs
nfl.team_stat_accounting_constraints.mechanism: Individual player outputs must sum to team outputs, so player legs on one team compete for a fixed pool, and incompatible leg sets have zero joint probability.
nfl.team_stat_accounting_constraints.rationale: Gaussian correlations allow two teammates to both hit first-TD legs or both clear very large yardage lines; the identity-based approach prevents impossible combinations and captures negative dependence among teammates.
nfl.team_stat_accounting_constraints.measurement: For each team-game and stat in {rushing yards, receiving yards, TDs, receptions} compute top-k player shares from the previous 17 games (half-life 8). Dirichlet-multinomial: concentration alpha_stat = a_team x (mean share vector over the 17 games) with a_team set by method of moments on the observed share variance, shrunk to the league alpha with weight 20 games; unlisted players get the residual 'other' category (floor of 5% of team total for yards). Sample team total from nfl.model_team_points_mean-based team stat model, allocate by Dirichlet-multinomial, output joint pairs of player legs (same-team) with sum(players) = team constraint. As-of previous game and latest inactive list.

team-game totals
nfl.team_stat_accounting_constraints.why: Directly handles same-team multi-leg combos that are the dominant retail leg set.

nfl.common_availability_shock.label: Shared availability shock across legs (QB, WR1, OL, kicker)
nfl.common_availability_shock.mechanism: One lineup event (QB scratch, kicker injury, star WR late scratch) moves several legs of the same combo simultaneously.
nfl.common_availability_shock.rationale: Legs priced early assume a baseline lineup; a late change lowers the QB yards leg, total and favourite-cover jointly, so the joint probability is a mixture over lineup states rather than a product.
nfl.common_availability_shock.measurement: Define lineup states (QB1/QB2, WR1 in/out, starting kicker, RT in/out) with probabilities from injury designation base rates (shrink to position-level, k=10 games); condition each leg on state using prior-season splits with k=3 games shrinkage; joint = sum over states of P(state) x product of conditional legs adjusted by in-state dependence. As-of per injury report vintage.

nfl.common_availability_shock.why: Late news makes combos stale unevenly; the mixture decomposition is needed to price the correlated move.

nfl.leg_void_push_matrix.label: Per-leg void, push and overtime state matrix
nfl.leg_void_push_matrix.mechanism: Each leg type has deterministic rules for pushes, postponement, no-snap voids and overtime that define the joint event and its payout.
nfl.leg_void_push_matrix.rationale: Combo payoff differs between a pushed leg being dropped or the combo lost; near 3 and 7 on integer spreads the push mass is 6-9% of games and cannot be ignored.
nfl.leg_void_push_matrix.measurement: Table with columns: leg_series, includes_OT (yes/no/unknown), push_possible (integer line), void_rule, fair_price_rule, source text hash and date; join to the combo's rules text; for each combo, compute P(joint | rule variant) for each variant of the unknown combo wording and carry the spread as model uncertainty. As-of rules text version captured at order time.

nfl.model_team_points_mean.label: Market-free team expected points and margin (drive-model mean and SD per team)
nfl.model_team_points_mean.mechanism: Each team's expected points are expected drives times points per drive, built from opponent-adjusted offence and defence efficiency, tempo, kicker and quarterback status and weather, with no betting line, price or implied total used as a feature.
nfl.model_team_points_mean.rationale: Market-derived team means (spread and total splits) are benchmarks that already contain the market's injury, weather and sharp information; feeding them into a model of the same game makes the model unable to show any independent information and hides which fundamental channels are missing. A market-free mean keeps the availability, weather, matchup and coaching channels explicit and lets the line be used only as an evaluation benchmark.
nfl.model_team_points_mean.measurement: For team i vs opponent j, expected points = E[drives_i] x E[points per drive_i]. E[drives] = 3600 / (mean seconds per drive implied by both teams' neutral-situation seconds per play and expected plays per drive), 2015+ regular-season pbp, ridge-shrunk 50/50 toward league mean at 8 games. Points per drive from a ridge regression on own opponent-adjusted offensive EPA per play (exponential half-life 8 games, prior-season carryover weight 0.3 decaying to 0 by week 10), opponent defensive EPA per play, red-zone TD rate (shrunk k=30 trips), kicker FG-range rating, starting-QB indicator, wind above 15 mph and dome flags, home indicator. Output team mean, SD (from residuals by tercile) and the margin and total means as differences and sums. As-of timestamp: after the previous game and re-run at the latest injury report. Betting lines are excluded from the feature set and used only for after-the-fact benchmarking.

nfl.model_margin_lattice.label: Model-based regulation margin lattice with mass at zero (key-number corrected, end-of-game behaviour included)
nfl.model_margin_lattice.mechanism: Probability that the regulation margin equals k, especially k=0, from a drive-outcome simulation or lattice centred on the market-free team means, corrected for the excess mass that 3-point and 7-point scoring and late tie-forcing behaviour put on small margins.
nfl.model_margin_lattice.rationale: Tie, overtime and integer-spread markets are priced on atoms at specific margins, which a smooth normal density misses; a lattice centred on betting-line residuals would import the market's own view of the game. Centring on the model mean margin and total from the market-free team means keeps the input market-free and lets the line serve as a benchmark only.
nfl.model_margin_lattice.measurement: Simulate 20,000 games per matchup from per-drive outcome multinomials (TD with 94 percent extra-point conversion, FG, safety, no score) calibrated so team means equal the market-free model team means, then fit an isotonic correction of simulated P(margin=k) to empirical regulation-margin frequencies (all regular-season games since 2002, about 5,500, binned by model |mean margin| in 0-3, 3-6, 6-10, 10+ points and model total terciles) with Beta(a=2, b=30) shrinkage in each bin for k=0 and Dirichlet smoothing for key numbers 3, 6, 7, 10, 14. Add an end-of-game term for tied games where the team with the ball inside two minutes can run the clock. Output P(margin=k) for k from -30 to 30. As-of: latest model means at kickoff minus 90 minutes; no spread, total or price enters.

nfl.model_margin_lattice.why: Key-number atoms and push probabilities for spread and total legs built around model means rather than line residuals.

nfl.leg_dependence_by_model_regime.label: Leg-pair dependence by model margin and total regime
nfl.leg_dependence_by_model_regime.mechanism: Cross-leg dependence (favourite cover with QB yards, total over with rusher yards) changes sign between competitive, blowout and shootout regimes; the regime must be assigned from the model's own pregame expectation.
nfl.leg_dependence_by_model_regime.rationale: One correlation coefficient averages positive shootout dependence with negative blowout dependence. Assigning regimes by the betting spread would make the combo price depend on the market line; using the model margin keeps the input market-free and lets the model disagree with the line.
nfl.leg_dependence_by_model_regime.measurement: For each leg-type pair (about 30 types), estimate Kendall tau or tetrachoric correlation of the two leg indicators within bins of the as-of pregame model expected margin from nfl.model_team_points_mean (|m|<3, 3-7, >7 points) and terciles of the model expected total, on 2015+ player-games with the model means re-computed point-in-time; shrink each bin toward the pooled estimate with k=150 games, require 400+ games per cell, report standard errors; as-of end of previous week. Closing spreads and totals are excluded and used only to benchmark.

nfl.cross_league_futures_leg.label: Cross-league futures leg marginal and dependence
nfl.cross_league_futures_leg.mechanism: A cross-league championship combo is the product of an NFL title probability and another league's title probability, adjusted for any shared dependence (near zero) and for the different resolution dates.
nfl.cross_league_futures_leg.rationale: The NFL leg comes from the season simulation, but the other leg (NBA champion) is outside every NFL input; without an explicit import of that sport's model output, with its own as-of time, the combo cannot be priced. Dependence between the legs is close to independence but resolution timing makes early NO paths matter for mark-to-market.

nfl.cross_game_leg_dependence.label: Residual dependence between win legs of different games on one slate
nfl.cross_game_leg_dependence.mechanism: Correlation between the outcomes of different games after conditioning on each game's model win probability, arising from shared model error, shared weather fronts and league-wide officiating trends.
nfl.cross_game_leg_dependence.rationale: Multi-game moneyline parlays are priced as a product of legs; if residual outcome correlation is non-zero (e.g. the model systematically overrates favourites in one week or one weather regime), the product misprices the parlay. Expected to be near zero, but must be measured rather than assumed because errors compound across 3 legs.
nfl.cross_game_leg_dependence.measurement: For every pair of games in the same week 2012-2025 (regular season and playoffs separately), compute residuals e_g = 1{home win} - p_model_g using point-in-time model win probabilities from nfl.model_margin_lattice (OT included, ties scored 0.5); estimate the pooled pairwise correlation of e_g within week, and conditional on both games outdoor with forecast wind >15 mph and on both favourites p>0.7; shrink toward 0 with a prior of n0=2000 pairs; output rho and its standard error per regime, as-of previous season.

nfl.combo_shared_weather_leg_coupling.label: Shared-weather common shock coupling same-game combo legs (total, kicker, passing, rushing)
nfl.combo_shared_weather_leg_coupling.mechanism: One kickoff-hour weather state (sustained wind, gusts, heavy precipitation, extreme cold) at an open-air venue shifts several legs of the same combo in fixed directions at once: it lowers the game total and team totals, lowers kicker points and long-FG legs, lowers QB passing-yard and receiver-yard legs, and raises rushing attempts and the leading back's carry legs.
nfl.combo_shared_weather_leg_coupling.rationale: Legs are priced from marginals that each absorb the weather forecast separately; multiplying them treats a 20 mph wind as an independent shock per leg, which understates the joint probability of same-direction combos (under + QB-yards under + kicker under) and overstates mixed-direction combos (over + QB-yards over). The effect is thresholded (near zero below about 10 mph sustained, steep above 15) and vanishes for domes and closed retractable roofs, so it is a regime variable, not a constant correlation.
nfl.combo_shared_weather_leg_coupling.measurement: For each open-air game 2010-2025 take the forecast weather state W (sustained wind mph, gust mph, precipitation flag, temp F) from nfl.weather_pit at the leg quote vintage (observed game-time weather from nflverse schedules for the historical fit, flagged as observed); roof in (dome, closed) sets W = calm. Bin W into calm (<10 mph, no precipitation), moderate (10-15 mph or light rain), severe (>=15 mph sustained or gusts >=25 or snow/heavy rain). For each leg pair type (game total x QB passing yards; game total x kicker points/long FG; QB passing yards x top receiver yards; game total x lead-rusher carries/yards; kicker points x team total) compute the residual of each leg statistic against its own-model expectation without the weather term (nfl.model_team_points_mean, qb/receiver/rusher projections), then the residual correlation and the weather-bin shift of both residual means; shrink bin correlations toward the calm-bin value with weight n/(n+80) leg-pairs. Joint simulation: draw W from the forecast distribution (forecast-error SD by lead time from archive vs observed), shift each leg mean by nfl.weather_total_response and the leg-specific weather slopes, and draw legs with the bin correlation. Output joint P(all legs) per combo and the weather share of the dependence. As-of the latest forecast vintage before the quote.

nfl.sibling_leg_marginal_interface.label: Cross-archetype leg output contract: per-leg P(yes) plus a shared latent game-state sample
nfl.sibling_leg_marginal_interface.mechanism: Defines what each sibling archetype model must export so combos can be priced coherently: the leg's marginal P(yes) and, for the same simulation draws, the latent game state (home and away points, margin, total, plays, starting QB and key-player availability state, weather bin) and the leg statistic itself, so joints are read from shared draws instead of a copula on marginals.
nfl.sibling_leg_marginal_interface.rationale: A combo is only as good as its marginals, and separate models that each simulate their own game state produce incoherent joints (a QB-yards draw from one game script paired with a cover from another). A fixed interface (fields, draw count, as-of time, seed alignment) is the definition that makes the combo layer reproducible; without it the cross-archetype dependency is undefined.
nfl.sibling_leg_marginal_interface.measurement: Interface spec, version 1. Producers: game_moneyline_spread, game_total, team_total, qb_passing_yards, receiving_yards_and_receptions, rushing_yards, anytime_first_td_scorer, first_half_and_quarter_totals. Each producer, for game g and as-of timestamp t (latest injury-report and forecast vintage before the quote), returns (a) for each listed leg: P(yes) under that leg's own settlement rule (OT in/out, push, DNP=0 or void) and (b) a draw matrix of S=20,000 simulations sharing a common seed per game: draw_id, home_pts, away_pts, regulation_home_pts, regulation_away_pts, ot_flag, team plays, QB1_active, key-player active flags, weather bin, and the leg statistic (yards, receptions, TD order). The game-level model (nfl.model_team_points_mean, nfl.model_margin_lattice) generates the shared columns; player archetypes condition on them. Consistency checks: mean of indicator over draws equals the exported P(yes) within 0.002; team-total and game-total draws obey home+away=total. Combos compute P(all legs) as the share of draws where every leg settles YES. Market prices are never inputs.

interactions.mechanism: The favourite's own QB passing yards and the favourite covering are positively linked in competitive shootouts, where passing builds the lead, but turn negative in blowouts where the leading team runs the clock; the underdog's QB yards are positively linked with the underdog scoring and negative with the favourite covering once the underdog trails. The sign depends on the margin regime and on whose QB is on the leg, so one fitted coefficient is wrong in both.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the pair correlation (favourite QB yards, favourite cover) and (underdog QB yards, favourite cover) separately for modelled |margin| bins and total terciles and test the sign change.

interactions.mechanism: Two receivers' yardage overs on the same team require a passing total that few games reach; the accounting identity makes the pair's joint probability much lower than the product conditional on the same team total, and zero for first-TD pairs.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare model joint for teammate pairs with and without the sum constraint on historical player-games.

interactions.mechanism: A QB scratch moves the favourite-win leg, team total and passing legs in the same direction but by different amounts; the combo's joint is a mixture over QB states whose weights are only known at inactive-list time.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest mixture-versus-product predictions on games with late QB changes.

interactions.mechanism: At integer lines on 3 and 7, a push leg changes the combo's payoff; the joint probability has a discontinuity at the key numbers and the effect depends on whether the push is dropped or loses.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute joint probability under both push rules for combos with lines on 3, 7 and 10; compare to settled outcomes.

interactions.mechanism: A favourite-covers-and-over combo requires the favourite to score roughly 27 or more, so the joint depends on the model margin and total means and on the lead-state script together rather than on each marginal alone; correlated margin and total residuals on the score lattice make the joint above the product when the favourite's offence drives both and below it when the favourite wins by defence and clock control.
interactions.how_to_test: On historical games compute the empirical joint of cover and over in bins of model margin mean and model total mean and compare with the product of marginals and with a lattice simulation using key-number mass.

interactions.mechanism: For multi-game moneyline parlays the error of the product approximation grows with the number of legs and with leg favouritism: a small positive residual correlation matters more when all legs are heavy favourites (joint near the product of large p) than for long-shot legs.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realized parlay hit rates against product-of-legs predictions binned by number of legs and minimum leg probability on 2012-2025 same-week game sets.

interactions.mechanism: Below about 10 mph the weather term barely moves any leg, so same-game legs are close to their script-only dependence; above about 15 mph sustained (or gusts near 25) total, kicker and passing legs all drop together, so the joint of an under/kicker-under/QB-under combo jumps above the product while an over/QB-over combo falls below it. Roofed games stay in the calm regime.
interactions.how_to_test: On 2010-2025 open-air games compute empirical joint hit rates of synthetic under+kicker-under and under+QB-yards-under pairs by wind bin and compare to the product of bin-specific marginals; repeat for dome games as the placebo.

nonlinearities.why: Correlation between the favourite covering and the QB's yards is positive in close games and negative in blowouts; averaging gives near zero and misses both.
Margin distribution has lumps at 3 and 7, so spread legs near these numbers have jump changes in cover and push probability that a continuous model does not produce.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in mean pairwise correlation at fixed marginals; bounded above by the smallest marginal
nonlinearities.why: For an all-legs-must-win combo the joint probability at fixed leg marginals rises convexly with the pairwise correlation and can never exceed the smallest marginal, so a misestimated correlation matters far more for long combos of positively linked legs than for mixed-sign legs.

contract.settlement_definition: 34 live series, all with rules text. Each market counts only points scored inside its named period: Q1-Q3 and the 1st half are regulation by construction; Q4 markets say '(excluding overtime)'; KXNFL2H, 2HTOTAL and 2HSPREAD say '(including overtime)', whereas KXNFL2HWINNER settles on 'the second half of regulation time' (overtime excluded). Totals are 'more than X.5' combined points, team totals 'over X.5' for one team, spreads 'wins by more than X.5' in the period; period-winner series (KXNFL1Q..4Q, 1H, 2H and the *WINNER series) are three-way with a Tie strike that resolves YES when the period score is level. BTTS series need points by both teams in the quarter (all scoring plays count); KXNFLEQBTTS needs both in every regulation quarter. KXNFLNOSCOREQ is YES if the teams combine for 0 points in any regulation quarter; KXNFLHIGHSCOREQ pays the highest-scoring regulation quarter, split 1/N among N tied quarters, OT ignored. KXNFL1HFT and KXNFLPREPACK1HFT are conjunctions of the halftime result and the full-game result (1HFT: 'including overtime'). Postponement: BTTS/1HFT series stay open if the game starts within 48 hours, else fair price; the *WINNER series stay open until the rescheduled game finishes 'within two weeks'.

mechanism.summary: Scoring in a period equals a small number of scoring events, each worth 3, 6, 7, 8 or 2 points, which happen when a possession finishes inside that window. The chain is (1) how many possessions start and finish in the period for each team: determined by the kickoff, the coin-toss deferral choice (which sets who starts Q1 and Q3), tempo, and clock burning; Q2 and Q4 also contain end-of-period tempo regimes; (2) the points per possession in that period, which differs by period because early drives are scripted, late-half drives are hurry-up with timeouts, and the fourth quarter is dominated by game state; (3) the discreteness of a quarter, in which 0, 3, 7, 10 and 14 absorb most of the mass and the two-team joint determines 0-0 and ties; (4) second-half periods being conditional on the halftime margin and on adjustments; and (5) contract specifics: regulation only, OT only in the 2nd half, ties settled by a Tie strike. A game-level total divided by four is a bad model because the distribution of drives and scoring is not uniform across quarters and quarter totals are lumpy.

stages.name: Possession allocation per period
stages.description: How many drives each team gets that begin in a given quarter depends on kickoff order, the second-half kickoff to the team that deferred, scoring that gives the ball back, and clock use. Q1 usually has 2 to 3 drives in total and Q2 3 to 4; a long first drive can consume most of Q1. At the end of a half, a team can run out the clock or force a final possession, so possession counts in Q2 and Q4 are state-dependent. Drive starts and ends should be tracked to the clock.
stages.distribution: Small count (1-5 drives per team per quarter), discrete; Q1 has especially few starts, producing a high zero-score mass

stages.name: Points per possession by period and script
stages.description: Efficiency in a quarter is not the game average: the first 15 scripted plays are rehearsed and tilt towards the offence's best plays, two-minute situations raise passing efficiency, the third quarter follows halftime adjustments, and the fourth quarter has prevent defences and clock-killing. Team strength (EPA) must therefore be carried into period-specific scoring rates with opponent adjustment and strong shrinkage since one team has ~3 drives per quarter.
stages.distribution: Per-drive Bernoulli-like outcomes (TD, FG, none) with period-specific rates; heavy small-sample noise at the team-quarter level

stages.name: Score lattice and tie mass
stages.description: A quarter's team score is mostly 0, 3, 6, 7, 10, 13, 14: a lattice with a spike at 0 for each team and a spike at equal scores for the two teams. Tie and 0-0 probabilities, BTTS and over/under 7.5 therefore depend on joint zero mass and increments. Over 7.5 requires at least a TD plus a point from either side or FG+FG+..., making it a lumpy event; this also generates strong key-number effects around 7 and 3. The whole-game anchor for the period allocation is the market-free team points mean (nfl.model_team_points_mean), so weather, availability and matchup channels enter the period expectation directly instead of through the market.
stages.distribution: Compound discrete distribution with atoms; P(0-0) is material in Q1 and Q3; ties are 10-20% in a quarter depending on scoring level

stages.name: Second-half state dependence
stages.description: Q3 and Q4 depend on the halftime lead: leading teams run more and shorten the game, trailing teams pass and press, and a large lead drives garbage time with backups. Q3 specifically also reflects the opening drive after halftime for the team that deferred. Because the margin is a latent variable only resolved after Q2, pregame quarter-3/4 totals are mixtures over halftime states. For the second-half contracts that count overtime (KXNFL2H, KXNFL2HTOTAL, KXNFL2HSPREAD) a tied regulation adds an overtime points term to the half total and can break a 2H tie, which is modelled as an explicit lattice term from nfl.ot_model. KXNFL2HWINNER is the exception: it settles on regulation only, so its Tie strike keeps the regulation tie mass that OT removes from KXNFL2H. The halftime/full-time contracts (KXNFL1HFT, KXNFLPREPACK1HFT) are the joint of the halftime state and the full-game winner, read directly off this halftime-conditional mixture.
stages.distribution: Mixture over halftime margin states; Q4 scoring is bimodal (competitive vs garbage time)

stages.name: Cross-period dependence and BTTS-every-quarter joint
stages.description: The probability both teams score in every one of four quarters is the joint of eight team-quarter events that are slightly positively associated through the common pace and quality of the offences and negatively through clock burn by a long drive. The product of marginals is not the correct joint.
stages.distribution: Joint over 8 dependent Bernoulli events; probability small, dominated by the weakest-scoring team-quarter

stages.name: Availability, rules and settlement
stages.description: A backup QB or missing key skill player changes early scripting and pace; period contracts count only points scored in the named period (the boundary attribution rule is not stated in the sampled text) with OT inclusion varying by market; ties settle on a Tie strike; postponement rules apply.
stages.distribution: Mostly deterministic given lineup states; QB status is a high-impact discrete mixture

stages.name: Quarter order statistics: highest-scoring and scoreless quarter
stages.description: KXNFLHIGHSCOREQ asks which of the four regulation quarter totals is largest, splitting the payout 1/N on ties; KXNFLNOSCOREQ asks whether the smallest quarter total is zero. Both are functionals of the joint distribution of four lumpy quarter totals, not of any single period. The second and fourth quarters carry structural advantages (two-minute drives before each half end, trailing-team urgency in Q4) so they win the argmax most often; Q1 and Q3 have fewer drives and a large 0-0 atom, so a scoreless quarter is usually Q1 or Q3 and is much more likely in low-total, bad-weather games. Ties at the top (e.g. 7-7 quarters) are common because totals sit on a 3/7 lattice, so the 1/N dead-heat mass must be modelled explicitly.
stages.distribution: Argmax and minimum over four dependent discrete lattice variables; top-quarter ties occur in a material share of games; P(any 0-point quarter) rises steeply as the expected game total falls

nfl.drive_clock_allocation.label: Drive-start allocation across periods (clock-resolved)
nfl.drive_clock_allocation.mechanism: The number of drives that begin in each quarter, and where the quarter ends relative to drive boundaries, for both teams.
nfl.drive_clock_allocation.rationale: Quarter totals depend on counts of starts and finishes in a 15-minute window; a game-level drives estimate ignores kickoff order, tempo by period, and clock burn.
nfl.drive_clock_allocation.measurement: From pbp: for each team-game, count drives starting in Q1..Q4 and seconds per drive by period; use 20-game recency weights (half-life 8) and opponent-adjust by regressing on opponent pace; combine with kickoff order to produce expected starts for each quarter and the probability of a second drive in Q1. Shrink to league mean with k=10 games.
raw_data: pbp: drive, qtr, drive_start_game_seconds_remaining, drive_end, drive_plays, posteam
nfl.drive_clock_allocation.why: Quarter markets have two or three drives; the allocation sets whether Q1 can host two scoring drives.

nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates.label: Opponent-adjusted per-drive TD/FG rates by period
nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates.mechanism: Per-drive probability of TD, FG and no score separately for Q1, Q2 (including two-minute drives), Q3 and Q4 by team and opponent.
nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates.rationale: Team quality is measured on all plays; period rates differ because scripted openers and hurry-up drills have different efficiency, and Q4 depends on game state; averaging understates the spread of per-quarter rates.
nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates.measurement: Multinomial (TD, FG, no score) logistic with team offence and opponent defence random effects per period, fitted on 3 seasons with exponential decay (half-life 12 team games); shrink period effects to the team's all-period rate with k=30 drives; as-of previous game; exclude garbage-time Q4 drives (win probability <5% or >95%) from the training sample and treat them separately.
raw_data: pbp: game_id, drive, qtr, drive_result (fixed_drive_result), posteam, defteam, wp
nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates.why: Directly feeds the period-specific scoring distribution rather than a game-average rate.

nfl.period_zero_tie_mass.label: Zero-score and tied-period mass by quarter
nfl.period_zero_tie_mass.mechanism: Empirical and model probabilities of 0-0 in a quarter, an equal non-zero score, and BTTS by quarter.
nfl.period_zero_tie_mass.rationale: Tie strike, 'both teams score' and over 7.5 are determined by the atoms of the joint distribution, which a Gaussian or Poisson-total approximation badly misstates.
nfl.period_zero_tie_mass.measurement: From 2010-2025 regular-season quarters (regulation only) tabulate P(home pts=a, away pts=b) per quarter q in 1..4. Model: independent per-team quarter-points PMFs from nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates x nfl.drive_clock_allocation (drives per quarter), then add a Gaussian-copula correlation per quarter estimated from the data (shrink to pooled with k=300 games). Fix atoms at 0,3,6,7,10 by isotonic regression of simulated against empirical frequency within expected-total terciles (low <42, mid 42-48, high >48 model total). Report P(0-0), P(tie) and P(both score) per quarter; as-of kickoff using the pregame model inputs, refit once per season, never using the game's own quarters.

nfl.period_zero_tie_mass.why: Tie, BTTS and over 7.5 contracts settle on atoms.

nfl.cross_period_score_dependence.label: Cross-quarter dependence of team scoring
nfl.cross_period_score_dependence.mechanism: The correlation between a team scoring in quarter j and in quarter k, accounting for pace, quality and clock burn.
nfl.cross_period_score_dependence.rationale: Every-quarter BTTS and 1H/2H combos require the joint of period events, which differs from the product of marginals.
nfl.cross_period_score_dependence.measurement: Compute tetrachoric correlations of team-scored-in-quarter indicators across quarter pairs from 2015+ team-games, split by team offensive EPA tercile; compare to the independence benchmark; shrink pairwise estimates toward the pooled with k=300 games; as-of season-to-date.
raw_data: quarter score indicators per team-game
nfl.cross_period_score_dependence.why: BTTS every quarter and 1HFT use dependence across periods.

nfl.kickoff_rule_regime.label: Kickoff and touchback rule regime and return rates
nfl.kickoff_rule_regime.mechanism: League kickoff rules (dynamic kickoff, touchback spot, setup zone) set the starting field position for Q1 and Q3 drives and for post-score drives.
nfl.kickoff_rule_regime.rationale: Rule changes since 2024 moved touchback placement and return rates, shifting early field position and short-field scoring; models fit to older seasons carry stale starting-position values.
nfl.kickoff_rule_regime.measurement: Per-season distribution of starting yard line after kickoffs, touchback rate, return rate and return TD rate; effective expected starting field position by team returner (k=20 returns shrinkage); flag season of rule change and refit; as-of week.
free_sources: NFL rulebook and competition committee announcements
raw_data: pbp: kickoff_returner, kick_distance, touchback, yardline_100 after kick
nfl.kickoff_rule_regime.why: Opening and second-half drives depend on starting field position, which the rule regime changes.

nfl.model_team_points_mean.label: Market-free team expected points and margin (drive-model mean and SD per team)
nfl.model_team_points_mean.mechanism: Each team's expected points are expected drives times points per drive, built from opponent-adjusted offence and defence efficiency, tempo, kicker and quarterback status and weather, with no betting line, price or implied total used as a feature.
nfl.model_team_points_mean.rationale: Market-derived team means (spread and total splits) are benchmarks that already contain the market's injury, weather and sharp information; feeding them into a model of the same game makes the model unable to show any independent information and hides which fundamental channels are missing. A market-free mean keeps the availability, weather, matchup and coaching channels explicit and lets the line be used only as an evaluation benchmark.
nfl.model_team_points_mean.measurement: For team i vs opponent j, expected points = E[drives_i] x E[points per drive_i]. E[drives] = 3600 / (mean seconds per drive implied by both teams' neutral-situation seconds per play and expected plays per drive), 2015+ regular-season pbp, ridge-shrunk 50/50 toward league mean at 8 games. Points per drive from a ridge regression on own opponent-adjusted offensive EPA per play (exponential half-life 8 games, prior-season carryover weight 0.3 decaying to 0 by week 10), opponent defensive EPA per play, red-zone TD rate (shrunk k=30 trips), kicker FG-range rating, starting-QB indicator, wind above 15 mph and dome flags, home indicator. Output team mean, SD (from residuals by tercile) and the margin and total means as differences and sums. As-of timestamp: after the previous game and re-run at the latest injury report. Betting lines are excluded from the feature set and used only for after-the-fact benchmarking.
free_sources: nflverse pbp and schedules (EPA, drives, seconds per play, wind, roof)
nflverse injuries and depth charts (QB status)
raw_data: pbp: drive, epa, points by drive, drive time, wind, roof
team-week starting QB and injury status
nfl.model_team_points_mean.why: Market-free whole-game team points mean (with weather, QB and matchup channels) from which period scoring expectations are allocated.

nfl.halftime_margin_scoring_model.label: Second-half scoring by halftime margin with model-based state weights
nfl.halftime_margin_scoring_model.mechanism: Q3 and Q4 scoring depend on the halftime margin and each team's script response; pregame 3Q, 4Q and 2H contracts are mixtures over halftime states.
nfl.halftime_margin_scoring_model.rationale: The same team scores differently leading by 14 than trailing by 3. The mixture weights must come from the model's own pregame margin so period prices are not anchored to the betting spread; second-half markets that include overtime also need the tie branch.
nfl.halftime_margin_scoring_model.measurement: Condition historical Q3 and Q4 team points on halftime margin bins (<=-10, -9..-4, -3..+3, +4..+9, >=+10) and on the point-in-time model expected full-game margin from nfl.model_team_points_mean (bins |m|<3, 3-7, >7); kernel-weight by halftime margin (bandwidth 3 points) and shrink to team second-half scoring with k=15 games; pregame mixture weights over halftime states from the first-half projection of nfl.model_margin_lattice; 2009+ pbp; as-of start of week. Spreads and totals excluded, used only as benchmarks.
raw_data: pbp: score at half, Q3/Q4 scoring per team
point-in-time own model expected margin
nfl.halftime_margin_scoring_model.why: Defines the state mixture for 3Q, 4Q and 2H contracts without a market input.

nfl.quarter_total_order_statistics.label: Joint four-quarter total distribution: argmax quarter (with dead-heat share) and P(minimum quarter = 0)
nfl.quarter_total_order_statistics.mechanism: Simulated joint distribution of the four regulation quarter totals from drive allocation and period-specific per-drive scoring, summarised as P(quarter q is the unique or shared maximum, weighted 1/N) and P(any quarter total = 0).
nfl.quarter_total_order_statistics.rationale: Highest-scoring-quarter and scoreless-quarter contracts depend on order statistics of four dependent, lumpy totals; marginal quarter totals cannot price them because ties at the top and zero atoms dominate, and Q2/Q4 two-minute effects make the quarters non-exchangeable.
nfl.quarter_total_order_statistics.measurement: Run >=20,000 drive-level simulations per game using period drive counts (nfl.drive_clock_allocation), period per-drive TD/FG/safety rates (nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates) and the halftime-state mixture for Q3/Q4; for each draw compute T_q (combined points, regulation only, OT excluded), payout_q = 1{T_q = max}/#{argmax}, and 1{min_q T_q = 0}; average. Calibrate against 2012-2025 empirical frequencies by expected-total decile (isotonic on P(min=0) and on Q2/Q4 argmax shares). As-of: inputs frozen at the Friday injury report plus kickoff weather forecast.

nfl.q_scoring.reason: Direct measure of period scoring but historical shares ignore opening-possession order and opponent drive allocation; use as a prior, not a point estimate. Its catalog measurement scales shares by the market game total; here shares scale the market-free nfl.model_team_points_mean.

nfl.opening_script.reason: Applies to Q1 only (and the first drive after halftime); high noise, so shrink heavily.

nfl.opening_possession.reason: Decides who starts Q1 and Q3 and who ends Q2; effect is real but modest and mostly captured by drive allocation.

nfl.two_minute_tempo.reason: Governs the end of Q2 and Q4 where timeouts and clock stops produce extra scoring chances. The catalog measurement takes lead/trail states from the spread; here they come from nfl.model_margin_lattice.

nfl.script.reason: Relevant to Q3 and Q4 but needs the halftime-state mixture to be usable for pregame pricing; the catalog's spread-implied state weights are replaced by the market-free model margin.

nfl.garbage_time.reason: Q4 only; sign depends on which side leads; treat as a regime in the state mixture. The P(14+ lead in Q4) step must use the model margin lattice, not the spread/total as the catalog text says.

nfl.team_total_split.reason: Implied team points from spread and total are market-derived and bring in the market's weather and lineup knowledge; replaced as the whole-game anchor by the model-based nfl.model_team_points_mean and kept only as an evaluation benchmark for the period allocation.

nfl.pace.reason: Neutral pace is a poor guide to Q1 and Q4 plays; use period-resolved clock allocation instead.

nfl.coaching.reason: Halftime adjustments and 4th-down aggression change Q3 and Q4, but no sourced coach-by-period measure exists; effect small.

nfl.kicker.reason: FG range converts stalled drives to 3 points, which is the second most common period score; matters most in low-scoring Q1.

nfl.ot_model.reason: Four live sampled contracts include overtime (KXNFL2H, KXNFL2HTOTAL and KXNFL2HSPREAD say '2nd half (including overtime)'; KXNFL1HFT's full-game leg is 'including overtime'), so OT points and tie-after-OT enter the second-half lattice; irrelevant for the regulation quarter and 1st-half contracts and for KXNFL2HWINNER, which settles on the second half of regulation time; KXNFLPREPACK1HFT does not state its OT treatment.

nfl.score_resid.reason: Defined as the score residual around market lines and key numbers, so it is market-derived; it is not a stage input here and period atoms come from nfl.period_zero_tie_mass (verdict corrected from WEAK by reverify-NFL-a).

nfl.qb.reason: A backup QB changes both early scripting and scoring rate; a discrete mixture variable. The catalog measurement values the QB change in points 'estimated from market line moves'; that market-derived valuation is not used here, the starter/backup gap comes from market-free efficiency inputs.

nfl.injuries_pit.reason: Matters through QB and a handful of key players; generic injury counts add little to period totals.

nfl.off_epa.reason: Season-level EPA is shrunk heavily for a single quarter; more informative via period-specific per-drive rates.

nfl.def_epa.reason: Same caveat as offence; only a small share of its variance shows up in a 3-drive quarter.

nfl.td_luck.reason: Regresses TD conversions that dominate quarter totals; partially duplicates points_vs_expected but useful here.
