interactions.mechanism: If a team receives the opening kickoff and runs a long scripted drive, Q1 can contain only one drive for the other team, so P(both score in Q1) falls while P(over 7.5) depends on whether the first drive ends in a TD; the effect is conditional on drive length.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Q1 BTTS and over 7.5 rates by receiving team and its first-drive length distribution.

interactions.mechanism: The team that deferred receives at halftime and can score at the end of Q2 and then again at the start of Q3, producing back-to-back scoring chances; the benefit is larger for coaches who use timeouts aggressively and for strong two-minute offences.
interactions.how_to_test: Test 2Q + 3Q scoring for the deferring team versus others controlling for team quality.

interactions.mechanism: Q4 totals are bimodal: close games produce hurry-up and late FG attempts (more scoring), while two-score leads shorten the game and lower scoring; the pregame total is a mixture whose weights come from the model's distribution of halftime and late-game margins.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate Q4 scoring by model expected-margin bucket and halftime-lead bucket; test bimodality and whether the mixture weights from the model lattice calibrate.

interactions.mechanism: A single FG changes a quarter from 0 to 3 and crosses neither 7.5 nor tie; but two FGs or one TD pass 7.5 only with additional scoring, so O/U 7.5 probability depends on a joint of kicker range and red-zone TD rate that is threshold-like.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare P(over 7.5) for team-quarters with equal expected points but different TD/FG mix.

interactions.mechanism: A backup QB cuts efficiency and tends to shorten drives, reducing both points per drive and drives; the two effects multiply in quarter scoring, with a larger proportional effect in Q1 where scripts are heavier.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Q1 totals for games with a backup QB vs starter with pace controls.

interactions.mechanism: P(scoreless quarter) is not linear in the expected game total: below roughly 38 combined expected points a 0-0 Q1 or Q3 becomes likely, while above about 50 it nearly vanishes; the argmax share also concentrates on Q2 as totals rise because two-minute drives add points mainly in high-efficiency games.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin 2012-2025 games by model expected total and plot empirical P(min quarter = 0) and Q2/Q4 argmax shares; test for a kink versus a logistic-linear fit.

nonlinearities.shape: atoms at 0 and at equal scores
nonlinearities.why: Quarter scores are not near-continuous; zero for each team and equal score pairs hold large probability, so smooth normal approximations misprice tie and BTTS strikes.

nonlinearities.shape: regime step above a lead threshold
nonlinearities.why: Once the lead exceeds about 17 in the 4th quarter, scoring behaviour changes discontinuously because starters leave and teams run the clock.

nonlinearities.shape: step at the effective range boundary
nonlinearities.why: FG probability drops sharply beyond the kicker's range (50-plus yards), so stalled drives past midfield convert to 3 points only in a narrow band that varies by kicker.

contract.settlement_definition: Three live series, all with rules text. KXNFLFIRSTTDTEAM resolves YES for the team that scores the game's first touchdown of any kind ('All touchdowns count ... including offensive, defensive, and special teams'); a first TD in overtime still counts, and 'No team scores a TD' resolves YES if no TD is scored in the full game including overtime. KXNFLFIRSTTDTIME is a time-bucket contract on when the first TD occurs; the sampled strike is 'record the first touchdown in the overtime period', so overtime is a bucket; the regulation bucket boundaries and the clock convention are not in the sampled text. KXNFLRACE resolves YES for the team that is first to score N points (sampled N=35) in the full game including overtime, with a 'Neither team' strike if neither reaches N. Postponed games starting within 48 hours stay open; otherwise fair price (FIRSTTDTEAM, RACE). Source: official final result/scoring summary.

mechanism.summary: The first score is a first-passage problem on a drive-level race. Teams alternate possessions after the kickoff; each possession ends in one of a few outcomes (touchdown, field goal, punt, turnover, turnover on downs, safety, end of half) with probabilities that depend on the team's offence, the opposing defence, starting field position and, for the first one or two drives, the coach's scripted plays. The first team to produce a TD (or reach N points) wins; the clock time of that event is the sum of the durations of the drives before it, so the time distribution depends on drive durations, which are right-skewed, and on how many drives pass before the first score. Non-offensive scores (pick-six, return TD, safety) arrive on a different, rarer hazard. Race-to-N markets add a lattice problem: points come in packages of 3, 6, 7, 8 and 2 and the first team to cross N depends on the order of TDs and FGs, not just the number of scoring drives. Because the first possession goes to one team, small advantages in first-drive TD probability compound into a first-score edge.

stages.name: Possession order and early-drive scheduling
stages.description: After the opening kickoff the receiving team has the first possession; the toss winner's choice (receive/defer) and kickoff rules decide this. Possessions then alternate subject to scores and turnovers. The probability that a team has the ball for the first, third and fifth drives determines how many early chances it has before the opponent can respond; the order gives a modest but systematic edge to the receiving team that compounds when drive-level TD probabilities are high.
stages.distribution: Binary draw (receive/defer) then alternating renewal process; cumulative drive counts by game clock differ by up to one drive between teams

stages.name: Per-drive outcome with scripted early drives
stages.description: Each drive's outcome is multinomial. Early drives differ from average because the coach scripts the first 10-15 plays; the first drive's TD rate and the shape of the call mix are not predictable from season EPA alone. Opposing defence quality, red-zone TD conversion and kicker range decide TD versus FG. Starting field position after the kickoff (touchbacks, returns) also shifts this probability.
stages.distribution: Multinomial per drive: TD, FG, no score, turnover, safety; a first-drive TD rate near one in five to one in four for typical teams with heavy variation across offences

stages.name: Drive duration and the time-of-first-TD clock
stages.description: The time of the first TD equals the sum of elapsed time over earlier non-scoring drives plus the scoring drive's own duration. A TD drive consumes about 4 to 6 minutes on average with wide dispersion; short fields and explosive plays end quickly. Pace, run rate and fourth-down policy determine the duration of failed drives. Time buckets (for example, 0-10 minutes, 10-20) therefore have mass shaped by a convolution of right-skewed durations, with discrete jumps at quarter ends. KXNFLFIRSTTDTIME also lists an overtime bucket, so the no-TD-in-regulation mass (roughly 1% of games or fewer; frequency not verified here) must be split by the overtime model into an OT-first-TD bucket and the no-TD case.
stages.distribution: Sum of right-skewed (lognormal-like) durations over a geometric number of drives; heavy right tail in time to first TD

stages.name: Non-offensive scores and turnovers
stages.description: Defensive and special-teams touchdowns, safeties and short fields after turnovers produce scores without an offensive drive completing. They have a low rate per game (roughly 15-20% of games contain a defensive or special-teams TD, a recollection-level estimate consistent with game_events g5, not verified here) but they pre-empt the offensive race and add mass to very early times; a turnover on the first drive creates a short field for the opponent. The mass of 'no TD in regulation' is split by nfl.ot_model: under the sampled KXNFLFIRSTTDTEAM text a first TD scored only in overtime still resolves the team strike Yes, and 'No team scores a TD' needs a TD-less overtime too, with the overtime possession rules of the season in force.
stages.distribution: Rare-event Poisson with low rate; turns first-score mass towards the early minutes and toward the defence

stages.name: Race-to-N points lattice
stages.description: KXNFLRACE pays the first team to score N points in the full game including overtime, or 'Neither team'. The winner depends on the sequence of scoring packages: TD (6-8 points), FG (3), safety (2), so P(team A first to N) is a path probability on a lattice driven by the TD/FG split, extra-point success and two-point tendency. At the sampled rung N=35 the dominant term is whether either team reaches 35 at all (the right tail of each team's points, roughly a 10-20% event for one team), so the race needs each team's full points distribution plus the order of crossing when both get there; low rungs are order-dominated. Package probabilities come from the model drive-outcome input, not from market lines.
stages.distribution: Compound renewal-reward process on a 2/3/6/7/8 lattice; for high N a first-passage probability dominated by the team-points tail, with a large Neither atom

stages.name: Contextual modifiers, availability and settlement
stages.description: Weather affects early FG versus TD decisions; QB or skill-player availability changes first-drive scripts; the rule text decides what counts as a score and the no-score case. Because the markets are early-game, only pregame information is relevant and lineup uncertainty at kickoff is a key mixture. nfl.qb is used for starter status only; its catalog QB point value estimated from market line moves is not used.
stages.distribution: Context shifts to drive probabilities; settlement is deterministic from the scoring summary

contract.settlement_definition: Seven live series, all with rules text. KXNFLTIE resolves YES if neither team wins and the game ends in a tie (NO if either team wins). KXNFLOT resolves YES if the game 'goes to overtime', i.e. is level after regulation. KXNFLSFTY resolves YES if either team records a safety, overtime safeties counting. KXNFLDSTTD resolves YES if either team records at least one defensive or special-teams touchdown, overtime counting. KXNFLTOTALTD and KXNFLGAMETD resolve YES if both teams together record at least N touchdowns (8+, 9+; floor 7.5/8.5), TOTALTD stating overtime TDs count while GAMETD's sampled text is silent on overtime. KXNFLTEAMTD resolves YES if one named team records N+ touchdowns (e.g. 'Green Bay: 4+', floor 3.5); its text does not mention overtime or TD type. Games postponed but started within 48 hours stay open, otherwise fair price (stated in every sampled text except KXNFLGAMETD, which has no postponement clause). Source: official final result / scoring summary.

Overtime rule era (verified from 2025 league-meeting reports): regular-season OT gives both teams a possession since 2025, stays 10 minutes, and can still end in a tie; the first team can win on a drive that consumes the full period. Seasons 2017-2024 used the 10-minute first-possession-TD-wins format, so P(level | OT) must be fitted by rule era.

mechanism.summary: These markets are rare or count events built from the same drive process, each with its own generator. A tie requires the game to be level after regulation and then level after overtime: P(tie) = P(regulation tie) x P(overtime ends level). Regulation ties come from the margin lattice (mass at zero, boosted by the 3/7 increments and end-of-game management), while the overtime ending depends on the OT rule set, each team's scoring rate and 4th-down policy in a 10-minute period. A safety is a count of rare special events: an offence is tackled or commits a foul in its own end zone, a punt or kick leaves the end zone, a snap or fumble goes out of bounds; the rate scales with plays run near its own goal line, pass rush versus protection, and punting from deep. A game touchdown count is the sum of the two teams' TD counts, each drives times TD-per-drive plus a small defensive and return TD rate, positively dependent through pace and shootout states, with overtime TDs included. Overtime occurrence is the regulation-tie atom itself. A defensive or special-teams touchdown is a rare hazard driven by takeaways, return opportunities and returner/coverage quality, and a single team's TD count ladder is that team's drives times TD-per-drive plus its own non-offensive TD rate.

stages.name: Regulation tie mass at zero margin
stages.description: P(tied after four quarters) depends on the final-margin distribution evaluated at zero, which has more mass than a smooth normal density implies because scores come in 3s and 7s and late-game kneeling or FG-for-tie decisions sit at zero. Tight spreads and low totals concentrate probability at small margins; coaches who are tied late may play for overtime. The margin atom comes from the model-centred lattice (nfl.model_margin_lattice) built on the market-free team means, never from line residuals. KXNFLOT is priced directly off this atom (P(level after regulation)), so g1 alone settles the overtime market.
stages.distribution: Discrete mass on the integer margin lattice; P(zero) a few percent of games with sensitivity to totals and lines

stages.name: Overtime resolution and the level-after-overtime event
stages.description: Since the 2025 season the regular-season overtime follows the playoff possession rule: each team gets a possession (an opening-drive touchdown no longer ends the game), then sudden death, inside a single 10-minute period after which the game is a tie. The team receiving first can still win without the other team touching the ball if its opening drive uses the whole 10 minutes and scores, and a second team trailing late in the period may run out of clock. A touchdown that wins the game outright ends it with no try (Super Bowl LVIII ended 25-22 on a walk-off touchdown), so the final OT margin is set as follows: after nothing or a FG by the first team, a second-team TD wins by 6 or 3 and a second-team FG wins by 3 or ties; after a first-team TD plus try (6, 7 or 8), a second-team FG loses by 3, 4 or 5, and a second-team TD that only ties or trails is followed by a try, leaving margins of 1 or 2 or a tie that continues into sudden death; unanswered first-team TDs end 6-8; sudden-death scores end 3 (FG), 6 (TD, no try) or 2 (safety). The game ends level only when the period expires with equal scores. P(level | OT) therefore depends on clock use and two-point decisions of both coaches, team TD/FG rates per drive, kickers and weather, and differs materially from the 2017-2024 first-TD-wins regime.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli given overtime with rule-era dependence; final OT margin on the lattice {1,...,8} with mass concentrated at 3 and 6-8; level outcome a few percent of OT games

stages.name: Safety hazard from end-zone exposure
stages.description: Safeties occur when the offence runs plays inside its own 5-yard line (sacks, intentional grounding, holding, tackles for loss on runs, fumbles through the end zone) or on special teams (blocked or errant punts and kicks). The rate is the number of exposed plays times a per-play safety probability that depends on pass rush win rate, offensive line, QB sack avoidance and defensive front. Rate per game is low (a few percent) so team-level estimation is noisy and requires pooling.
stages.distribution: Rare-event Poisson with rate from end-zone exposure; zero-inflated at the team level

stages.name: Game and team touchdown counts from the TD pools
stages.description: KXNFLTOTALTD/KXNFLGAMETD count every touchdown by either team (offensive, defensive, return; overtime explicitly for TOTALTD) and KXNFLTEAMTD counts one team's touchdowns. Each team's count is expected drives times TD-per-drive (red-zone conversion and 4th-and-goal policy decide TD versus FG) plus a low-rate non-offensive TD hazard. The two teams' counts are positively dependent: a fast, efficient game gives both offences more possessions and a trailing team keeps throwing. Game rungs such as 8+/9+ and team rungs such as 4+ sit in the right tail, so overdispersion and between-team dependence matter more than the means.
stages.distribution: Team count: overdispersed integer with mean about 2-3 TDs; game count: sum of two positively correlated counts, right-skewed; 8+/9+ game and 4+ team rungs are upper-tail events

stages.name: Defensive and special-teams touchdown hazard
stages.description: KXNFLDSTTD pays if either team scores a defensive or special-teams touchdown (interception or fumble return, punt or kick return, blocked kick return), overtime included. The game rate is roughly one such TD every five to six games. It is the sum of two team hazards, each the opponent's giveaway rate times return-TD conversion plus kick/punt return opportunities times returner threat and opposing coverage quality. Turnover-prone QBs, high pressure rates, wet weather and a trailing opponent forced to throw raise it; the kickoff rule regime (touchback rate) controls return volume.
stages.distribution: Rare-event Poisson per team-game with a small rate; game-level P(>=1) roughly 0.15-0.2, heavily driven by realized turnovers, which are mostly noise

stages.name: Participation, void and rule application
stages.description: All live series here are team or game events, so there is no named-player void; the rule that matters is the 48-hour postponement clause (fair-price settlement) and which window counts: safeties, D/ST TDs and KXNFLTOTALTD include overtime, the tie market is the post-overtime result, the overtime market is the regulation result, and GAMETD/TEAMTD are silent on overtime. The source is the official scoring summary; a stat correction can relabel a TD's type (offence vs return), which matters for KXNFLDSTTD.
stages.distribution: Deterministic rule application with a small probability of correction; participation is a discrete mixture

nfl.late_tie_game_management.label: Late-game tie-state management policy
nfl.late_tie_game_management.mechanism: In the last two minutes with the score level, trailing by 3 or leading by 3, coaches choose between kneeling, kicking a game-winning FG, or pushing; these decisions concentrate regulation margin mass at 0.
nfl.late_tie_game_management.rationale: The margin distribution at zero is partly behavioural: a team tied with the ball inside two minutes may run the clock to guarantee overtime, and a team trailing by 3 kicks a tying FG. A smooth score model misses this.
nfl.late_tie_game_management.measurement: From pbp: for each coach and season, rate of kneel-downs, FG attempts and go-for-it when score diff in {-3..0} and game_seconds_remaining<=120; shrink to league with k=10 occasions; compute P(tie at final | state) by state and apply to the simulated margin distribution; as-of previous week.
raw_data: pbp: score_differential, game_seconds_remaining, qb_kneel, field_goal_attempt, timeouts
nfl.late_tie_game_management.why: Behaviour at the end of regulation moves the zero-margin atom, which sets both tie and OT markets.

nfl.ot_ending_hazard.label: P(game ends level | overtime) under current OT rules
nfl.ot_ending_hazard.mechanism: Probability that the overtime period fails to produce a decisive score under the rule era in force: from 2025 in the regular season both teams get a possession inside a 10-minute period followed by sudden death, so a level finish needs equal scores (no score, matched FGs, matched TDs and tries) when the clock expires.
nfl.ot_ending_hazard.rationale: Overtime ending level is a very small but rule-dependent event; the tie market is the product of two small probabilities and the OT-rule change makes historical frequencies stale.
nfl.ot_ending_hazard.measurement: Simulate OT as a drive process with a 10-minute clock (regular season) and the possession rule of the season's era (2017-2024 first-possession TD wins; 2025+ both teams possess unless the opening drive uses the full period and scores, then sudden death); per drive TD/FG/safety/empty rates and drive duration from the two teams' drive-level data shrunk to league with k=150 drives; a try only after a TD that does not end the game (walk-off TDs have none), with extra-point versus two-point choice from coach policy; 4th-down aggression. Level outcome = period expires with equal scores (no score, matched FGs, matched TD plus equal try). Calibrate to realized regular-season OT outcomes per era since 2012; report P(level | OT) with credible interval; as-of start of season and refreshed weekly.
free_sources: nflverse schedules and pbp (overtime flag, result)
raw_data: pbp: qtr==5 plays, drive results, game result
rulebook version by season
nfl.ot_ending_hazard.why: Needed because the tie market equals OT probability times this hazard; the existing ot_model lacks an explicit definition.

nfl.endzone_exposure_plays.label: End-zone exposure plays per team-game
nfl.endzone_exposure_plays.mechanism: Count of offensive plays run with the ball inside the team's own 5-yard line and punts from within the own end zone or 5, which are the sites of most safeties.
nfl.endzone_exposure_plays.rationale: Safeties scale with exposure; a team that starts drives deep and has a poor punt unit has several times more exposed plays than another.
nfl.endzone_exposure_plays.measurement: From pbp: per team-game count of offensive plays with yardline_100>=95 plus punts with yardline_100>=90, with a per-play safety probability by play type (sack, run, pass, punt) from 2010+ league data, team factor shrunk with k=30 exposed plays; recency half-life 20 games; expected safeties = sum count x probability; as-of previous game.
raw_data: pbp: yardline_100, play_type, sack, safety, punt_blocked
nfl.endzone_exposure_plays.why: Provides the opportunity count for the rare event rather than relying on team-level safety counts that are mostly zero.

nfl.rush_yardage_tail.label: Per-carry yardage tail (explosive-run probability) by rusher
nfl.rush_yardage_tail.mechanism: Mixture distribution of rushing yards per carry for the named player: P(10+), P(20+), P(40+) per carry after opponent adjustment.
nfl.rush_yardage_tail.rationale: The maximum over N carries is governed by tail probabilities, not average yards per carry; two backs with equal averages have different longest-rush distributions.
nfl.rush_yardage_tail.measurement: For rushers (RB and QB separately) fit a discrete tail: P(yards>=k per carry) for k in {7, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40} on 3 seasons of carries, half-life 25 carries; shrink to positional prior with k=60 carries; adjust by opponent run-defence tail rate (stuff and explosive-allowed) with k=100 carries; as-of previous game.
free_sources: Next Gen Stats rushing (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for public access)
raw_data: pbp: rusher_player_id, rushing_yards, yardline_100, defenders_in_box
nfl.rush_yardage_tail.why: Defined for KXNFLLONGRSH, which the market-universe reconciliation moved to rushing_yards; not staged in this archetype any more and kept only so the catalog definition stays traceable.

nfl.carry_count_forecast.label: Named-player carry count distribution by script
nfl.carry_count_forecast.mechanism: Forecast distribution of the player's number of carries given team spread, game script, role and injury designation.
nfl.carry_count_forecast.rationale: N, the number of draws for the maximum, is overdispersed; a leading team gives the back 25 carries, a trailing team 10; zero for no-play voids.
nfl.carry_count_forecast.measurement: Carries ~ NegBin with mean = team rush attempts x carry share. Team rush attempts: mean by bucket of own-model expected margin (nfl.own_team_rating_market_free, no spread or total) in bins <=-7, -7..-3, -3..3, 3..7, >=7 using 2016-2025 games, team effect shrunk with k=8 games. Carry share: snap-weighted share over last 8 games, half-life 6, shrunk to depth-chart role prior with k=3 games. Dispersion by role (RB1, RB2, QB) fit by maximum likelihood on player-games with share >=10 percent; P(0 carries) = P(inactive) from nfl.injuries_pit plus P(active, zero carry) from NB. As-of final inactive list.
raw_data: player-game carries and snaps
team rush attempts by game state
own pre-game margin from nfl.own_team_rating_market_free
inactive list
nfl.carry_count_forecast.why: Defined for KXNFLLONGRSH, which the market-universe reconciliation moved to rushing_yards; not staged in this archetype any more and kept only so the catalog definition stays traceable.

nfl.model_team_points_mean.label: Market-free team expected points and margin (drive-model mean and SD per team)
nfl.model_team_points_mean.mechanism: Each team's expected points are expected drives times points per drive, built from opponent-adjusted offence and defence efficiency, tempo, kicker and quarterback status and weather, with no betting line, price or implied total used as a feature.
nfl.model_team_points_mean.rationale: Market-derived team means (spread and total splits) are benchmarks that already contain the market's injury, weather and sharp information; feeding them into a model of the same game makes the model unable to show any independent information and hides which fundamental channels are missing. A market-free mean keeps the availability, weather, matchup and coaching channels explicit and lets the line be used only as an evaluation benchmark.
nfl.model_team_points_mean.measurement: For team i vs opponent j, expected points = E[drives_i] x E[points per drive_i]. E[drives] = 3600 / (mean seconds per drive implied by both teams' neutral-situation seconds per play and expected plays per drive), 2015+ regular-season pbp, ridge-shrunk 50/50 toward league mean at 8 games. Points per drive from a ridge regression on own opponent-adjusted offensive EPA per play (exponential half-life 8 games, prior-season carryover weight 0.3 decaying to 0 by week 10), opponent defensive EPA per play, red-zone TD rate (shrunk k=30 trips), kicker FG-range rating, starting-QB indicator, wind above 15 mph and dome flags, home indicator. Output team mean, SD (from residuals by tercile) and the margin and total means as differences and sums. As-of timestamp: after the previous game and re-run at the latest injury report. Betting lines are excluded from the feature set and used only for after-the-fact benchmarking.
free_sources: nflverse pbp and schedules (EPA, drives, seconds per play, wind, roof)
nflverse injuries and depth charts (QB status)
raw_data: pbp: drive, epa, points by drive, drive time, wind, roof
team-week starting QB and injury status
nfl.model_team_points_mean.why: Market-free team means (hence mean margin and total) that locate the regulation-tie and overtime probabilities without line-implied inputs.

nfl.model_margin_lattice.label: Model-based regulation margin lattice with mass at zero (key-number corrected, end-of-game behaviour included)
nfl.model_margin_lattice.mechanism: Probability that the regulation margin equals k, especially k=0, from a drive-outcome simulation or lattice centred on the market-free team means, corrected for the excess mass that 3-point and 7-point scoring and late tie-forcing behaviour put on small margins.
nfl.model_margin_lattice.rationale: Tie, overtime and integer-spread markets are priced on atoms at specific margins, which a smooth normal density misses; a lattice centred on betting-line residuals would import the market's own view of the game. Centring on the model mean margin and total from the market-free team means keeps the input market-free and lets the line serve as a benchmark only.
nfl.model_margin_lattice.measurement: Simulate 20,000 games per matchup from per-drive outcome multinomials (TD with 94 percent extra-point conversion, FG, safety, no score) calibrated so team means equal the market-free model team means, then fit an isotonic correction of simulated P(margin=k) to empirical regulation-margin frequencies (all regular-season games since 2002, about 5,500, binned by model |mean margin| in 0-3, 3-6, 6-10, 10+ points and model total terciles) with Beta(a=2, b=30) shrinkage in each bin for k=0 and Dirichlet smoothing for key numbers 3, 6, 7, 10, 14. Add an end-of-game term for tied games where the team with the ball inside two minutes can run the clock. Output P(margin=k) for k from -30 to 30. As-of: latest model means at kickoff minus 90 minutes; no spread, total or price enters.
free_sources: nflverse schedules/results (final regulation scores by quarter)

interactions.mechanism: Regulation tie probability needs the pregame margin to be small and total low, because with fewer scoring drives the probability mass at exactly zero rises; the effect is concentrated at model expected margins under 3 and totals under the mean.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(regulation tie) by model mean-margin and model-total bucket against a smooth normal model and against the lattice.

interactions.mechanism: When tied in the last two minutes a coach with ball may run the clock to force overtime, which makes a regulation tie probability above what a lattice model gives; this behaviour differs by coach and applies only in a narrow state.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare empirical regulation tie rates against lattice prediction by coach policy tercile.

interactions.mechanism: Safety probability equals exposed plays times per-play sack/penalty rate; an offence that starts many drives deep faces a pass rush that wins often, so exposure and rush win rate multiply rather than add.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress safeties on exposure x opposing pressure rate product.

interactions.mechanism: The game TD count is the sum of two team counts that share pace and shootout states: when both offences are efficient each extra possession for one side is also one for the other, so P(total >= 8) is well above the product of independent team tails; overtime adds a further TD chance only in tied games, which are more likely when both means are similar.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare empirical P(game TDs >= k) for k = 6, 7, 8 with an independent-Poisson sum built from the two model team TD means, binned by combined model mean; estimate the residual between-team correlation.

interactions.mechanism: Wind above a threshold of roughly 15 mph or very cold temperatures cut overtime FG reliability and stall drives, raising the chance that overtime ends level; below the threshold the effect is negligible, so the response is a regime switch applied to P(level | OT), not a continuous effect on regulation ties.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare OT outcomes in weather regimes using playoffs and regular season OT games.

interactions.mechanism: A defensive touchdown needs a takeaway and a return to the end zone; the takeaway count scales with the opponent QB's turnover-worthy play rate and with pressure, and the return conversion with field position and defender speed, so the D/ST TD probability rises with the product of pressure and giveaway propensity, not their sum.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit per team-game pick-six and fumble-return TD counts against opponent turnover-worthy play rate, pressure rate and their product on 2016-2025 pbp; compare deviance.

nonlinearities.shape: convex upper tail in the combined TD mean
nonlinearities.why: For a high rung such as 8+ total TDs, the probability rises convexly with the sum of the two team TD means (and faster still with positive between-team dependence), so a one-TD error in the combined mean moves deep rungs by a large relative amount.
With rates of a few percent per game the probability is near linear in lambda, but team differences in lambda arise from exposure counts, not from observed rare outcomes.

Tie = P(OT) x P(level | OT): each factor is small and uncertain; relative errors multiply, so the tie market is the most sensitive to rule changes. Note the P(level | OT) factor is a rule-era input; the OT margin lattice is wider than 0, 3, 6 when both teams possess (a TD plus extra point can leave a 1 or 2 point margin).

contract.settlement_definition: Six live series; four have rules text (KXNFLGAME, KXNFLSPREAD, KXNFLWINMARGIN, KXNFLPROBOWL), two are TITLE_ONLY (KXNFLPROBOWLWIN, KXNFLWEEKHIGH). KXNFLGAME (moneyline) resolves YES for the team that wins; 'If the game ends in a tie, the market will resolve to $0.50 for each team', and postponed games not started within 48 hours settle at a fair price. KXNFLSPREAD is 'wins by more than X.5 points' (half-point strikes, no push; overtime not mentioned). KXNFLWINMARGIN settles on the point differential 'in the full game (including overtime)' with exact-margin strikes ('exactly 0' = tie after OT). KXNFLPROBOWL resolves YES if the named conference (NFC/AFC) wins the Pro Bowl flag football game. KXNFLWEEKHIGH (week's highest-scoring game) and KXNFLPROBOWLWIN have no sampled text; their tie-splitting and settlement are not verified. Source: the official final result.

variants_and_edge_cases: Tie handling differs: KXNFLGAME pays $0.50 to each team on a tie; KXNFLWINMARGIN has an 'exactly 0' strike (full game incl. OT); KXNFLSPREAD 'wins by more than X.5' simply resolves NO for a tie; spread text does not mention overtime.
Only the 35.5 rung of KXNFLSPREAD was sampled; ladders presumably also list competitive rungs (not verified), and a 35.5-point rung is priced entirely by the far tail of the margin distribution.

KXNFLWEEKHIGH (title only) is a maximum over the week's slate of game totals; dead-heat handling is not visible. The season blowout series and the former week-game-high ticker are no longer filed here.

KXNFLPROBOWL/PROBOWLWIN are all-star exhibitions in a flag-football (Pro Bowl Games) format with conference rosters; whether skills-event points carry into the 'flag football game' result is not stated.
Postponement: KXNFLGAME states the 48-hour fair-price rule; SPREAD and WINMARGIN sampled texts do not.

mechanism.summary: The final margin M = (home points - away points) is the sum of a structural expectation and a heavy-tailed, lattice-valued noise term. The structural mean is team quality difference (offence and defence, QB-weighted, regressed from preseason priors and updated through the season) plus home-field edge plus situational shifts (rest, travel, weather, motivation), then adjusted at kickoff by the actual lineup: the QB, offensive line, pass rush and secondary starters. The noise is not Gaussian: scores come in discrete packages so the margin has spikes at 3, 6, 7, 10, 14; its variance depends on total scoring, pace, weather and QB volatility; and its tails are heavier than normal because of blowout snowballing (turnovers, garbage time) and rare events (defensive TDs). Moneyline probability is the mass above zero (with ties and overtime assigned by the wording); each spread rung is a tail probability of the same distribution, so a ladder is a monotone curve whose far rungs are determined by tail shape. The week's highest-scoring game is a maximum over the slate's game totals, and the Pro Bowl conference winner is a separate exhibition process with selected rosters, opt-outs and flag-football rules.

stages.name: Structural team-strength difference
stages.description: The expected margin starts with the strength of both teams: offence and defence efficiency adjusted for opponent, with recency weighting, preseason priors from returning production and an in-season updating rule. The effective rating of each team depends on who is playing, so ratings need a lineup layer. Rating noise itself is a source of uncertainty (state-space process noise) that widens the margin distribution.
stages.distribution: Gaussian-like estimate with uncertainty about 2 points in margin for each team's rating; mean difference sets the margin location

stages.name: Lineup and unit adjustments at kickoff
stages.description: Starting QB is the largest single change (a replacement-level QB is worth several points of margin and raises margin variance); offensive-line absences, pass-rush injuries and secondary absences change specific matchups (pass rush against protection, coverage against route concepts). These arrive as timestamped reports (Wednesday to inactive list), so the pregame margin is a mixture over lineup states until about 90 minutes before kickoff.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over QB and unit states; position-weighted points adjustments; inactive list collapses mixture

stages.name: Environment and situational shifts
stages.description: Home-field edge varies by team and by travel and rest; a short week or cross-country early kickoff shifts the mean by a point or less; weather lowers scoring (and thus margin variance) and favours the run; stakes and rest decisions late in the season change effort and starter participation.
stages.distribution: Small mean shifts (tenths to one point) and variance changes; regime effects in extreme weather and in week 17-18 rest

stages.name: Margin distribution: lattice, variance and tails
stages.description: Given the mean, the margin distribution has a lattice with spikes at 3 and 7, a standard deviation of roughly 13 points that varies with the total and with the lineup state, and heavier tails than a normal. Heteroskedasticity matters: a 38-point total game has a narrower margin distribution than a 52-point one. Probabilities of covering integer lines and of exact-margin buckets are read off this lattice; deep rungs (20-35 points) depend on the tail model. Atoms and tails are centred on the market-free model means (nfl.model_team_points_mean), not on line residuals.
stages.distribution: Discrete non-Gaussian with key-number atoms; variance heteroskedastic; tail heavier than normal

stages.name: Overtime, ties and settlement mapping
stages.description: The moneyline settles a tie at $0.50 per team, so its fair value is P(win incl. OT) + 0.5 x P(tie after OT); win-margin includes overtime and puts the tie in the 'exactly 0' bucket; a spread rung resolves NO on a tie and its text is silent on overtime. Overtime collapses margins to small values (3, 6, 7 or 0 under sudden death; with both teams possessing, 1 or 2 are also possible, and the format in force is unverified), so the OT model moves the regulation zero-margin atom (about 6% of games) to small margins and leaves about 0.4% as ties.
stages.distribution: Mass transfer from zero margin to +/-1..7 after OT; deterministic mapping by wording with half-payout on moneyline ties

stages.name: Ladder coherence and aggregate order statistics
stages.description: Spread ladders are cumulative tails of one distribution, so rung probabilities must decline monotonically and deep rungs are priced as tail, not as extrapolation of the body. KXNFLWEEKHIGH (title only) is the maximum of 13-16 game totals in a week, which needs each game's total distribution, their shared-weather dependence and the slate composition (byes, international and Monday games).
stages.distribution: Monotone ladder of tail probabilities; maximum-of-N over the weekly slate's game totals with heterogeneous means

stages.name: Pro Bowl flag-football exhibition
stages.description: KXNFLPROBOWL (and title-only KXNFLPROBOWLWIN) pay on the conference that wins the Pro Bowl flag football game. The process shares nothing with regular-season margins: rosters are fan/player/coach-voted selections thinned by injury opt-outs and Super Bowl participants, the game is non-contact 7-on-7 flag football with short fields, so QB passing accuracy and receiver/defensive back speed dominate, and effort is low and variable. With few games in this format, the outcome is close to a coin flip shifted by the realized roster quality, especially which quarterbacks actually play.
stages.distribution: Single Bernoulli near 0.5 with modest shifts from roster quality; very small history in the flag format, so heavy shrinkage to 0.5

nfl.lineup_adjusted_team_rating.label: Lineup-adjusted team rating (position-weighted value over replacement)
nfl.lineup_adjusted_team_rating.mechanism: Team margin rating is rebuilt each week as a sum of position-weighted player values over replacement for the players expected to play, rather than a team average.
nfl.lineup_adjusted_team_rating.rationale: Team EPA averages blend games with and without key starters; the effective rating for a given Sunday depends on who is active, which is known (partially) at known timestamps. Position weights differ greatly: QB, OT, EDGE, CB1 matter more per player than interior positions.
nfl.lineup_adjusted_team_rating.measurement: For each position slot s (QB, LT, RT, C, G, TE, WR1-3, RB, EDGE1-2, DT, LB, CB1-2, S) estimate weight w_s as the ridge coefficient (lambda chosen by season-blocked cross-validation) from regressing team game margin residuals (actual margin minus the own rating_state_space expectation) on indicators for the starter being active, 2015-2025. Player value above replacement v_p = w_s x (index_p - index_replacement), where index is EPA/play on field shrunk to the position mean with k=400 snaps and replacement is the backup's snap-weighted index. Team lineup adjustment = sum over expected active starters of v_p; no market-derived quantity enters. As-of each injury report vintage and the inactive list.
free_sources: nflverse rosters, injuries, depth charts, snap_counts
raw_data: injury vintages, depth chart, snap counts, team game margins
player performance indices
nfl.lineup_adjusted_team_rating.why: Converts the injury and depth data into an explicit margin adjustment; absent from the current list, which treats availability as a flag.

nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd.label: Conditional margin variance model
nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd.mechanism: Standard deviation and shape of the final margin as a function of expected total, spread magnitude, pace, weather and QB state.
nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd.rationale: The fixed SD of 13 points misprices tails: a low-total, windy game has a narrower margin distribution than a shootout; cover probability at +/- 10 differs by regime for the same mean.
nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd.measurement: Fit quantile regression (or location-scale model with t-distributed errors) of final margin on the model mean margin and model total from nfl.model_team_points_mean (not betting lines), wind, dome, backup-QB flag and divisional flag, with data 2010+ (about 4,500 games); report conditional SD and 5/95% tail multipliers; refit annually; as-of pregame values. Betting lines are excluded from the feature set and used only to benchmark the fitted SD after the fact.
raw_data: game results, wind, temp, roof, backup-QB flag
model mean margin and total per game
nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd.why: Needed to convert any mean into cover and win probabilities consistently across rungs and regimes.

nfl.deep_tail_margin_model.label: Blowout tail model for margins above 21 points
nfl.deep_tail_margin_model.mechanism: Extreme-margin probability as a function of mismatch, QB state, turnover snowballing and weather.
nfl.deep_tail_margin_model.rationale: Deep rungs (20+) and season-maximum blowout contracts are priced on the tail and a normal fit materially understates them; the distribution of margins above 28 across 2000+ is thick.
nfl.deep_tail_margin_model.measurement: Fit generalized Pareto (threshold 21) to |margin| for 2000+ games with covariates: |model expected margin| bucket from nfl.model_team_points_mean, backup QB, model total; estimate shape xi with bootstrap CI; expected number of games above k in a season = sum over games of P(|M|>k); for season max compute 1 - prod(1 - p_g); as-of start of week.
raw_data: final scores 2000-2025
model mean margin and total per game
nfl.deep_tail_margin_model.why: Prices deep KXNFLSPREAD rungs (e.g. 35.5) and large WINMARGIN buckets that live entirely in the tail.

nfl.slate_total_extremes.label: Slate-level highest-total and largest-margin order statistics
nfl.slate_total_extremes.mechanism: Joint distribution of the week's game totals and margins, for maxima and tie-splitting.
nfl.slate_total_extremes.rationale: The highest-scoring game market and weekly max margin are maxima over 13-16 games with heterogeneous means; ties split the payout so exact integer ties matter.
nfl.slate_total_extremes.measurement: For each slate game g draw total from the game-total distribution (mean from nfl.pace/off_epa model, SD from nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd analog for totals), include shared weather correlation (rho from nfl.corr), simulate 20,000 slates; report P(game g has highest total) and expected payout under $1/N split; as-of kickoff vintages for each game.
raw_data: game total distributions, slate composition (bye weeks), weather
nfl.slate_total_extremes.why: Prices KXNFLWEEKHIGH (week's highest-scoring game), a slate maximum that a single-game model cannot price.

nfl.rating_state_space.label: Team-strength state-space updating rule (preseason prior, process noise, opponent adjustment)
nfl.rating_state_space.mechanism: Team ratings are latent states updated weekly with an offseason regression to the mean and weekly process noise, with opponent adjustment simultaneously solved.
nfl.rating_state_space.rationale: Different updating speeds produce different mid-season ratings; slow updating misses real changes, fast updating chases noise; the choice is rarely defined in the catalog.
nfl.rating_state_space.measurement: Kalman filter on a 64-dim state (off and def EPA/play rating per team). Season boundary: state = rho x last-season final state + (1-rho) x league mean, rho estimated by regressing year t+1 final ratings on year t (2005+), expected about 0.5-0.6; preseason prior variance = residual variance of that regression. Weekly process variance sigma_p^2 estimated by marginal likelihood on 2005-2025. Observation = team-game opponent-adjusted EPA/play (offence and defence separately) with observation weight w = 1 for plays with 0.05<=wp<=0.95 (no-spread wp) and 0.2 otherwise. Output posterior mean and variance per team as-of previous week; refit walk-forward.
raw_data: pbp: epa, posteam, defteam, wp, week
nfl.rating_state_space.why: Defines how ratings stay current and carries rating uncertainty into the margin variance.

nfl.model_team_points_mean.label: Market-free team expected points and margin (drive-model mean and SD per team)
nfl.model_team_points_mean.mechanism: Each team's expected points are expected drives times points per drive, built from opponent-adjusted offence and defence efficiency, tempo, kicker and quarterback status and weather, with no betting line, price or implied total used as a feature.
nfl.model_team_points_mean.rationale: Market-derived team means (spread and total splits) are benchmarks that already contain the market's injury, weather and sharp information; feeding them into a model of the same game makes the model unable to show any independent information and hides which fundamental channels are missing. A market-free mean keeps the availability, weather, matchup and coaching channels explicit and lets the line be used only as an evaluation benchmark.
nfl.model_team_points_mean.measurement: For team i vs opponent j, expected points = E[drives_i] x E[points per drive_i]. E[drives] = 3600 / (mean seconds per drive implied by both teams' neutral-situation seconds per play and expected plays per drive), 2015+ regular-season pbp, ridge-shrunk 50/50 toward league mean at 8 games. Points per drive from a ridge regression on own opponent-adjusted offensive EPA per play (exponential half-life 8 games, prior-season carryover weight 0.3 decaying to 0 by week 10), opponent defensive EPA per play, red-zone TD rate (shrunk k=30 trips), kicker FG-range rating, starting-QB indicator, wind above 15 mph and dome flags, home indicator. Output team mean, SD (from residuals by tercile) and the margin and total means as differences and sums. As-of timestamp: after the previous game and re-run at the latest injury report. Betting lines are excluded from the feature set and used only for after-the-fact benchmarking.
free_sources: nflverse pbp and schedules (EPA, drives, seconds per play, wind, roof)
nflverse injuries and depth charts (QB status)
raw_data: pbp: drive, epa, points by drive, drive time, wind, roof
team-week starting QB and injury status
nfl.model_team_points_mean.why: Market-free team means (and hence mean margin and total) that locate the margin distribution and ladder rungs without line-implied inputs.

nfl.model_margin_lattice.label: Model-based regulation margin lattice with mass at zero (key-number corrected, end-of-game behaviour included)
nfl.model_margin_lattice.mechanism: Probability that the regulation margin equals k, especially k=0, from a drive-outcome simulation or lattice centred on the market-free team means, corrected for the excess mass that 3-point and 7-point scoring and late tie-forcing behaviour put on small margins.
nfl.model_margin_lattice.rationale: Tie, overtime and integer-spread markets are priced on atoms at specific margins, which a smooth normal density misses; a lattice centred on betting-line residuals would import the market's own view of the game. Centring on the model mean margin and total from the market-free team means keeps the input market-free and lets the line serve as a benchmark only.
nfl.model_margin_lattice.measurement: Simulate 20,000 games per matchup from per-drive outcome multinomials (TD with 94 percent extra-point conversion, FG, safety, no score) calibrated so team means equal the market-free model team means, then fit an isotonic correction of simulated P(margin=k) to empirical regulation-margin frequencies (all regular-season games since 2002, about 5,500, binned by model |mean margin| in 0-3, 3-6, 6-10, 10+ points and model total terciles) with Beta(a=2, b=30) shrinkage in each bin for k=0 and Dirichlet smoothing for key numbers 3, 6, 7, 10, 14. Add an end-of-game term for tied games where the team with the ball inside two minutes can run the clock. Output P(margin=k) for k from -30 to 30. As-of: latest model means at kickoff minus 90 minutes; no spread, total or price enters.
free_sources: nflverse schedules/results (final regulation scores by quarter)
raw_data: games: home/away score by quarter, overtime flag
pbp: drive result, points, game_seconds_remaining
nfl.model_margin_lattice.why: Margin atoms at 3, 7 and zero for integer rungs, ties and win-margin buckets built around model means, not line residuals.

nfl.pro_bowl_flag_roster_strength.label: Pro Bowl flag-football conference roster strength (actual participants)
nfl.pro_bowl_flag_roster_strength.mechanism: Conference win probability in the Pro Bowl flag game as a function of the quarterbacks and skill players who actually participate after opt-outs and replacements.
nfl.pro_bowl_flag_roster_strength.rationale: The exhibition removes line play and contact, so passing accuracy and open-field speed of the participants decide most scoring; the official roster changes repeatedly after selection (injuries, Super Bowl teams), so only the final participant list is informative and the format history is tiny.
nfl.pro_bowl_flag_roster_strength.measurement: For each conference, take the final participant list at game time; compute QB score = mean regular-season completion percentage over expected and EPA/dropback of participating QBs (weighted by expected snaps, equal split if unknown) and skill score = mean of participating WR/TE/RB yards per route run, standardised across all participants; logit P(NFC) = b*(QB_diff + 0.5*skill_diff) with b shrunk toward 0 (prior sd 0.3) because only a handful of flag-format games exist; as-of the final roster announcement.
free_sources: NFL.com Pro Bowl roster and replacement announcements (free_scrape)
raw_data: Pro Bowl rosters by conference with replacement dates
regular-season QB CPOE and EPA per dropback, WR/TE yards per route run
Pro Bowl Games results by year
nfl.pro_bowl_flag_roster_strength.why: KXNFLPROBOWL is now a confirmed live series in this archetype and no regular-season side input applies to an all-star flag game.

nfl.ratings.reason: The catalog definition is power ratings and market-implied strength history; the market component makes it a benchmark that leaks the closing line into a model of the same game, so it is removed from stages, coverage and interactions in favour of nfl.model_team_points_mean and nfl.rating_state_space.

nfl.qb.reason: Largest single lineup effect; must be a mixture until inactives and combined with replacement-level performance. The catalog measurement values the QB change in points 'estimated from market line moves'; that market-derived valuation is not used here, the starter/backup gap comes from market-free efficiency inputs.

nfl.off_epa.reason: Structural margin component; opponent-adjusted but needs a defined state-space update and garbage-time weighting.

nfl.def_epa.reason: Same caveats; defensive EPA is noisier and less persistent than offensive.

nfl.pythag_luck.reason: Close-game and Pythagorean regression is a real overrating source for teams with fluky records.

nfl.turnovers.reason: Takeaway rates regress strongly; duplicates part of pythag_luck for turnover-driven records.

nfl.field_pos.reason: Special-teams and field position are persistent small margin contributors.

nfl.injuries_pit.reason: Timestamped designations drive lineup mixtures; value is conditional on mapping to position weights.

nfl.ol.reason: Offensive line absences are under-reflected in team averages; effect measurable at tackle and center.

nfl.rest_travel.reason: Systematic but small; interacts with kickoff time and venue.

nfl.venue.reason: Team-specific home edge, dome and surface; shrink team HFA heavily.

nfl.weather_pit.reason: Mainly changes variance and total, little mean effect on margin; only extreme wind/precipitation matter.

nfl.motivation_seeding.reason: Relevant in weeks 17-18 only; inapplicable earlier, so a small share of games.

nfl.score_resid.reason: Defined around market lines and key numbers; key-number mass is re-built around model means as nfl.model_margin_lattice, and the line-centred version is kept only to benchmark that lattice.

nfl.ot_model.reason: Controls zero-margin mass and OT mapping; needed for OT-inclusive and regulation-only wordings.

m.external_lines.reason: Sharp sportsbook prices are a benchmark for edge; listing them as a primary input would make the model a copy of the market.

m.rules_text.reason: Regulation versus OT, ties ($0.50 per team on KXNFLGAME, 'exactly 0' on WINMARGIN) and postponement define the event; SPREAD OT treatment and the two title-only series remain unverified.

m.ladder_structure.reason: The catalog defines this input as a smooth CDF fitted to rung prices (implied mean, SD and mass between rungs), i.e. a market-derived quantity; rung monotonicity is enforced by modelling one count or margin distribution, so the price-fitted ladder is kept only as a benchmark and removed from stages and coverage (reverify-NFL-a).

nfl.def_personnel.reason: Defensive injuries timing and effect; overlaps with coverage_scheme as the 'coverage scheme' half is duplicative.

nfl.divisional_familiarity.reason: Division rematch effect is small and unstable; the catalog itself says to test via residuals. Its catalog measurement regresses the residual versus spread/total, so it is market-referenced; removed from stage m3.

m.volume_oi.reason: Liquidity does not determine who wins by how much; it only bounds position sizes.

m.trade_tape.reason: Trade prints are market behaviour; may be used for microstructure analysis only.

nfl.pass_rush.reason: Pass-rush against pass-block is the largest unit matchup but needs interaction with OL and QB sack avoidance.

nfl.coverage_scheme.reason: Coverage shell and man/zone rates are not the same as defensive injury timing; the 'defensive scheme' wording overlapped but the QB and receiver archetypes use it as a distinct matchup input, so it is kept here as a secondary opponent-matchup input and the DUPLICATE_OF verdict withdrawn.

nfl.run_defense.reason: Run defence against a run-heavy offence affects clock and margin; effect moderate.

nfl.coaching.reason: 4th-down aggression raises variance; tempo changes the number of drives; effect on mean small.

interactions.mechanism: A backup QB lowers the mean margin and raises its variance and skews it; the cover probability at +3 and +10 changes differently from the moneyline since both location and scale move together.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit location-scale model with a backup-QB indicator and compare calibration at several rungs.

interactions.mechanism: Pass-rush win rate multiplies with offensive-line pass-block weakness and the QB's sack-avoidance; the interaction, not the sum, drives sacks and drive failures; strong rush against a weak tackle with a slow QB creates outsized damage.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress drive-success on rush win rate x pass-block rate x time-to-throw.

interactions.mechanism: High wind or heavy precipitation lowers totals and compresses margin variance, shifting cover probability for heavy favourites down and raising the underdog's cover probability; effect appears past a wind threshold around 15 mph.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare cover rates for favourites by wind bucket after controlling for rating difference.

interactions.mechanism: A west-coast team travelling east for an early kickoff on short rest loses a fraction of a point, but the effect is offset in domes and for teams used to travel; it is conditional on kickoff time and venue.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact kickoff hour with time zones crossed in a margin residual regression.

interactions.mechanism: Blowout probability rises convexly in the expected margin because turnovers snowball (short fields, garbage-time scoring); a team that is a 14-point favourite with a backup quarterback on the other side has a deep-rung probability several times higher than a linear extrapolation.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(margin>21) by expected-margin decile and compare to Gaussian prediction.

nonlinearities.why: Probability of covering a half-point line jumps when the line moves across a key number; the body of the margin distribution is lumpy, so linear rating-to-probability maps misprice rungs next to 3 and 7.

Win probability is a normal-CDF-like function of the model expected margin with SD around 13 points; the slope at a pick'em is far larger than at -10, so equal margin-mean errors cost much more near zero.
The QB effect is discrete: starter vs replacement differ by a large block of points, so the mean margin is a mixture of two modes rather than a smooth variable.

contract.settlement_definition: Three live series, all with rules text. KXNFLTOTAL and KXNFLTOTALPRECISE resolve YES if the two teams 'collectively score more than' a half-point strike (24.5 and 98.5 sampled), so no push; neither sampled text says whether overtime points count or states a postponement rule. KXNFLBOTH resolves YES if each team records at least N points (sampled N=35, strike_type greater_or_equal), with 'Points scored in overtime count'; postponed games starting within 48 hours stay open, otherwise fair price. mechanism.summary: The total is the sum of points from about 22 to 26 possessions. Think of it as plays times points per play, split into how many snaps the game contains and how many points each snap yields. The number of snaps is set by clock consumption: each play burns 5-7 seconds if inbounds and a few if incomplete, passing rates and incompletions stop the clock, timeouts and penalties shape late-half tempo, so the total plays are determined by both offences' pace and run rates and by the lead (a leader runs the clock). Points per snap depend on efficiency and field position, with TD/FG conversion near the goal line and turnovers that both end drives and shorten fields. Environment multiplies efficiency: wind, cold and precipitation reduce passing and kicking beyond thresholds, domes and altitude shift it the other way. The two teams' scores are positively correlated through shared pace and weather but negatively through clock-killing leaders. The result is a lattice-valued, right-skewed distribution with a mean near 44 points and heavy tails: some games score under 25 and some over 70, and ladders reaching 98.5 are priced almost entirely by the tail. Settlement wording (overtime included or not) shifts the distribution by the 6-7 percent mass of games that go to overtime.

stages.name: Number of plays and possessions from clock consumption
stages.description: The number of plays is determined by clock time: seconds per play depends on run/pass mix, incompletion rate, no-huddle use, timeouts and penalties; both teams' paces combine toward a mutual tempo, and the leading team slows the game. Possessions follow from plays per drive (drive length depends on efficiency) and from scoring/turnover frequency. This stage fixes the opportunity count for points. Coach and coordinator tempo and 4th-down policy (nfl.coaching) shift seconds per play, no-huddle use and the TD-versus-FG outcome of stalled drives, so they enter as a secondary plays-and-drive-ending input. The catalog nfl.two_minute_tempo measurement takes lead/trail states from the spread; here those states come from the market-free nfl.model_margin_lattice.
stages.distribution: Count of plays about 125 +/- 10; possessions 22-26; both right-skewed in shootouts; tempo mutual rather than additive

stages.name: Points per possession from efficiency and field position
stages.description: Points per drive depend on offensive EPA and success against the specific defence, starting field position (kickoff rule, punting, turnovers), red-zone TD versus FG conversion, explosive plays and kicker range. Finishing luck regresses to the drive-efficiency expectation, so recent scoring above expectation should not be extrapolated. Efficiency is correlated across the two teams only through shared environment.
stages.distribution: Points per drive about 2 with SD near 2.2 per drive; drive-level distribution (0, 3, 6/7/8) is discrete and zero-heavy

stages.name: Environment: weather, venue and roof
stages.description: Wind above about 15 mph cuts deep passing and long field-goal range, temperatures under freezing reduce passing and kicking efficiency, precipitation raises fumbles; domes and warm weather raise passing efficiency. Responses are thresholded, and forecast error is the real unknown pregame, so the weather effect is an expectation over forecast vintages rather than a point.
stages.distribution: Piecewise response with thresholds; forecast uncertainty adds a discrete mixture (calm vs windy)

stages.name: Lineup state and unit matchups
stages.description: QB status is a mixture that shifts both teams' points and pace; offensive line and pass-rush availability change sack rates, drive failures and pressure-driven turnovers; coverage injuries change completion efficiency. The total is therefore a mixture over lineup states until inactives. Short-week and post-bye rest (nfl.rest_travel) and late-season clinched or eliminated starter rest (nfl.motivation_seeding) change effective lineups and tempo.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over QB/line states; each component with its own mean and variance

stages.name: Joint distribution of the two scores and tails
stages.description: Home and away points are positively correlated through pace and environment and negatively through clock control by a leader and garbage time, so the variance of the total is not the sum of the variances. The distribution has key-number spikes (37, 41, 44, 47), a heavy right tail (turnover-fuelled blowouts, defensive TDs) and a lower tail (defensive slogs, wind). Deep rungs like 24.5 and 98.5 are tail events.
stages.distribution: Lattice-valued, right-skewed, SD near 10 points, with tail multipliers; key-number atoms

stages.name: Overtime inclusion and ladder coherence
stages.description: If overtime counts, a regulation tie (about 5-7% of games) adds roughly 3 to 10 points to the total; if it does not, the total is truncated. P(OT) is the regulation zero-margin mass of the market-free margin lattice and the OT points distribution comes from the rule-era overtime model. The ladder across rungs is one monotone survival curve of that mixture. The wording determines which of two distributions applies, so it must be resolved from the rules rather than inferred.
stages.distribution: Mixture of regulation and OT-extended distributions; monotone ladder constraint

stages.name: Both teams reaching a high threshold
stages.description: KXNFLBOTH pays only if each team scores at least N points (35 sampled), overtime included. That is the joint upper tail of two team scores: P(X_home>=35, X_away>=35). Each marginal is perhaps 10-15% for an average offence, and the joint is driven by shootout dependence (fast pace, weak defences, a trailing team forced to keep scoring), offset by the clock-killing of a comfortable leader. A blowout total of 70 can resolve NO, so this rung needs each team's own points distribution and their copula in the upper tail, not the total's survival curve. Overtime adds a few points to both only in tied games, mainly raising 35-35 style outcomes. The joint tail is read from nfl.paired_score_covariance_own, the shared joint home/away score pmf (a Student-t copula per expected-total and wind bin, so upper-tail dependence is estimated rather than assumed zero) over the marginals of nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean; the same joint feeds team totals and slate extremes. Its tail calibration at N = 28-42 against empirical joint frequencies remains to be tested (u5).
stages.distribution: Joint survival of two positively tail-dependent lattice counts; a small probability (low single digits percent for typical games) highly sensitive to upper-tail dependence

nfl.total_plays_state_model.label: State-conditional total plays model (mutual tempo with lead effects)
nfl.total_plays_state_model.mechanism: Total plays are a function of both teams' seconds per play, run rates, expected lead state and clock stoppages rather than the average of two neutral paces.
nfl.total_plays_state_model.rationale: Neutral pace is measured when the score is close; actual plays depend on how the game goes, and a favourite protecting a lead cuts plays substantially; the combination of two paces is not additive.
nfl.total_plays_state_model.measurement: Regress total plays per game (2015+) on both teams' rolling neutral seconds per play (last 10 games, half-life 5), PROE, own and opponent run rate, expected absolute margin (own model from nfl.own_team_rating_market_free, not market), rolling completion rate and penalty rate (all computed from games before the as-of week), with team and opponent random effects and ridge shrinkage; output expected plays and SD. Weather only via wind/dome flags from the kickoff forecast. As-of previous week; fit walk-forward.
raw_data: pbp: game_id, plays by team, seconds per play, qtr, score_differential, penalty
team neutral pace
nfl.total_plays_state_model.why: Turns two team paces into the number of snaps that the total actually counts.

nfl.total_distribution_tail.label: Both-tail model of game total points
nfl.total_distribution_tail.mechanism: Tail probabilities of the combined score beyond about 1.8 SD in each direction conditional on expected total and environment.
nfl.total_distribution_tail.rationale: TOTALPRECISE ladders extend to 98.5 and TOTAL to 24.5; these rungs are priced on tails, which a normal approximation gets wrong because totals are right-skewed with heavy upper tail from blowout cascades and short-field TDs. The expected total it conditions on is the market-free model total, so the tail does not inherit the line.
nfl.total_distribution_tail.measurement: Fit a shifted-lognormal (or NB-mixture) to 2000-2025 regular-season game totals conditioned on walk-forward expected total E_g in terciles (<40, 40-48, >48) and weather regime (calm/dome, wind>=15 or temp<32); for seasons before 2015 compute E_g with the ridge rating of nfl.own_team_rating_market_free (never a betting total), for 2015+ use nfl.model_team_points_mean. Add atoms at totals 37, 41, 43, 44, 47, 51 as residuals of a smoothed fit with Dirichlet smoothing. Report P(total >= 70) and P(total <= 24) with 5,000-game bootstrap CI; validate calibration by decile of E_g. As-of season start, refreshed weekly.
raw_data: final scores since 2000, wind, roof, model expected-total regime (market-free)
nfl.total_distribution_tail.why: Deep rungs are tail events; the existing key-number input does not define tails.

nfl.weather_total_response.label: Weather dose-response function for totals (wind, cold, precipitation, roof)
nfl.weather_total_response.mechanism: Estimated effect on expected total points of wind speed, temperature and precipitation categories with roof interactions.
nfl.weather_total_response.rationale: Weather effects are strongly nonlinear: below 10 mph wind is negligible, above 15-20 mph reduces totals by several points; forecast error needs to be handled at the pregame time. Historical fits use observed (not forecast) conditions until a season of forecast capture exists.
nfl.weather_total_response.measurement: Outcome = realized game total points minus own-model expected total from nfl.model_team_points_mean (never a betting total). Hierarchical regression on 2010+ games: wind piecewise-linear with knots 10, 15, 20 mph, temperature knots 32, 50 F, precipitation flag, dome flag, and bin random effects shrunk with k=100 games. Fit on observed game-time weather; at prediction time use forecast vintages at 24 h and 3 h pregame and propagate forecast error (estimated from archive vs observed) by errors-in-variables attenuation. As-of pregame forecast.
free_sources: nflverse schedules (wind, temp as measured at game)
raw_data: game-time observed wind/temp, forecast vintages, roof

nfl.weather_total_response.why: The existing weather input lists data fields but not the response function or the forecast-versus-actual issue.

nfl.model_team_points_mean.label: Market-free team expected points and margin (drive-model mean and SD per team)
nfl.model_team_points_mean.mechanism: Each team's expected points are expected drives times points per drive, built from opponent-adjusted offence and defence efficiency, tempo, kicker and quarterback status and weather, with no betting line, price or implied total used as a feature.
nfl.model_team_points_mean.rationale: Market-derived team means (spread and total splits) are benchmarks that already contain the market's injury, weather and sharp information; feeding them into a model of the same game makes the model unable to show any independent information and hides which fundamental channels are missing. A market-free mean keeps the availability, weather, matchup and coaching channels explicit and lets the line be used only as an evaluation benchmark.
nfl.model_team_points_mean.measurement: For team i vs opponent j, expected points = E[drives_i] x E[points per drive_i]. E[drives] = 3600 / (mean seconds per drive implied by both teams' neutral-situation seconds per play and expected plays per drive), 2015+ regular-season pbp, ridge-shrunk 50/50 toward league mean at 8 games. Points per drive from a ridge regression on own opponent-adjusted offensive EPA per play (exponential half-life 8 games, prior-season carryover weight 0.3 decaying to 0 by week 10), opponent defensive EPA per play, red-zone TD rate (shrunk k=30 trips), kicker FG-range rating, starting-QB indicator, wind above 15 mph and dome flags, home indicator. Output team mean, SD (from residuals by tercile) and the margin and total means as differences and sums. As-of timestamp: after the previous game and re-run at the latest injury report. Betting lines are excluded from the feature set and used only for after-the-fact benchmarking.

interactions.mechanism: A fast-paced team facing an opponent who runs the ball and burns clock gets fewer plays than its own pace implies; the product of the two teams' tempo preferences, not their average, determines total plays, and the effect is amplified when the leader runs more.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress total plays on the product and difference of team paces.

interactions.mechanism: Wind has little effect below about 12 mph then removes deep passing and long field goals sharply; the total falls by several points over a narrow range of wind speed, and the loss is larger for vertical offences and for teams reliant on 50-yard kickers.
interactions.how_to_test: Piecewise-linear regression of total residual on wind with knots at 10, 15, 20 mph.

interactions.mechanism: A backup QB changes efficiency and tempo together (more runs, fewer plays, shorter drives) and the total drops more than the efficiency change alone, but only when the opponent is a good defence; with a poor defence a backup can still score.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate total residual by QB status interacted with opponent defence tercile.

interactions.mechanism: Home and away scores correlate positively in shootouts and negatively through clock control; the variance of the sum and the tails depend on the regime, so a single correlation understates the upper tail in shootout conditions and overstates in blowouts.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate corr(home,away) by expected-margin and expected-total bucket.

interactions.mechanism: A team with a red-zone TD rate far above the league mean and unchanged EPA is projected to regress; the correction is larger for teams whose red-zone sample is small, and affects the total by roughly a point per team.
interactions.how_to_test: Out-of-sample test of regression with shrinkage constant against realized points.

interactions.mechanism: Tail dependence of the two scores is strongest when both expected team totals are high and the expected margin is small (a projected shootout) and turns negative-to-neutral when one side is a large favourite, because a big leader runs the clock and the trailing side's late points come against soft coverage but too few possessions to reach 35.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(both>=35)/(P(home>=35)P(away>=35)) by bins of expected total and |expected margin| on 2002-2025 games and test whether the ratio varies with |margin| at fixed total.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise linear with a knee near 15 mph wind
nonlinearities.why: Total points are nearly flat in wind below the knee and fall steeply above it; a linear weather coefficient underestimates storms and overstates mild wind.
The total distribution is right-skewed: games over 65 are much more frequent than a normal with SD 10 implies, and TOTALPRECISE-type rungs near 98.5 are far-tail events.

nonlinearities.shape: spikes at key totals (37, 41, 44, 47) on top of a right-skewed tail
nonlinearities.why: Probability of exceeding a half-point strike jumps when the strike crosses a key total, because 3- and 7-point packages concentrate mass on particular integer sums; smooth totals models misprice rungs adjacent to those integers.
Play counts are bounded by the 60-minute clock: increasing neutral pace beyond a point yields smaller increments in plays because stoppages and timeouts dominate.

contract.settlement_definition: Fourteen live series of non-game events, 13 with rules text (KXNFLCONTRACTSIZE is TITLE_ONLY). Each settles on an official act, list or occurrence: head-coach departure before a date, firing/resignation/announced exit (KXNFLCOACHOUT) and which coach is next out among all head coaches before Feb 15, 2027, interims excluded (KXNFLNEXTCOACHOUT); a named person hired as a coach in men's pro football before a date (KXNFLHIRECOACH); listing on the initial post-cutdown 53-man active roster, reserve/practice-squad lists excluded and later cuts not reversing YES (KXNFL53MAN); official team-announced or league-registered signing, media reports insufficient (KXNFLHKANE); retirement announcements effective before the next regular season (KXNFLRETIRE); a non-NFL athlete recording at least one snap, preseason included (KXNFLCOMPETE); supplemental-draft declaration confirmed before July 15 (KXNFLSUPDRAFTPICK); a trade officially processed and approved before a date, YES even if later rescinded (KXNFLTRADE); a player's next team before a date, with 'Retires / No Team' and stay-with-current-team outcomes (KXNFLNEXTTEAM); a team playing N+ primetime games (SNF, MNF, TNF plus Thanksgiving and Christmas, Wednesday opener excluded) (KXNFLPRIMETIME); any official weather delay of a game, including pre-start delays and in-game stoppages (KXNFLDELAY); and an international game beginning in the named city before a date, NO on cancellation or postponement past it (KXNFLGAMELOCATION).

rules_evidence.quote: Practice-squad and reserve-list designations, including injured reserve, physically unable to perform, non-football injury/illness, suspended, and exempt lists, do not count as inclusion on the 53-man active roster.
rules_evidence.establishes: The 53-man market is conditional on active-roster status on cut day; injured and suspended players are excluded even if they are on the club.

rules_evidence.quote: If the head coach of the Cincinnati Pro Football team leaves, or announces they will leave, before Mar 1, 2027
rules_evidence.establishes: The coach-out event includes announced future departures, so the hazard includes resignations and pre-announced exits, not only firings.

rules_evidence.quote: A signing must be officially announced by the team or registered by the NFL. Media reports of agreements or agreements in principle alone are insufficient.
rules_evidence.establishes: Signing contracts require an official announcement, so insider reports are information but not settlement.

rules_evidence.quote: The retirement must be intended to be effective immediately or prior to the first new regular season after the announcement.
