variants_and_edge_cases: Resolution source differs: official team/league announcement (signing, retirement, 53-man, coach exit, hire, trade processing), the published schedule and broadcast windows (primetime), an official weather delay, or venue of kickoff (game location). 'Announced vs reported' is explicit for signings.

Strike construction: per-candidate binaries (coach out, hire, trade), categorical outcome sets with residual strikes (next team incl. current team and 'Retires / No Team'; next coach out across all coaches), and count thresholds (5+ primetime games).

KXNFLTRADE resolves YES on official processing even if the trade is later rescinded or the player fails a physical; KXNFLGAMELOCATION resolves NO (not fair price) on cancellation or postponement past the date.

Coach and retirement series have an 'announces' clause, which front-loads resolution relative to the actual departure; KXNFLNEXTCOACHOUT excludes interim coaches and counts only departures after issuance.

KXNFLHIRECOACH counts any coaching hire 'in men's pro football' (wording could include coordinator roles or other leagues); KXNFLCONTRACTSIZE is TITLE_ONLY, so the value definition (total, APY, guarantees) is unknown.
Award specials, the Top 100 list, the on-air role series and draft-order markets are no longer filed here and are not claimed.

Blueprint-inherited context inputs (m.external_lines, nfl.award_voting_mechanics, m.quote_history) are benchmark-only or irrelevant here and are not used by any stage; nfl.award_voting_mechanics, nfl.broadcast_role_assignment and m.quote_history are detached by patch.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official league and team announcements, the league transaction wire (trades, signings, roster lists), the published NFL schedule and flex announcements, official game delay records, and venue of kickoff.

mechanism.summary: Off-field outcomes are generated by organisations, schedulers and the weather, not by plays. (1) Who decides: owners and general managers (coach exits and hires, signings, trades, cuts, contract offers), players and agents (retirement, free-agent destination, supplemental-draft declaration), the league office and broadcasters (schedule windows, flex, international venues), or physical conditions (lightning and severe weather). (2) What constrains them: contract terms and guarantee dates, the salary cap, roster limits and designation rules, the calendar (Black Monday, the trade deadline, cut-down day, free agency, schedule release, flex windows) and the standings. (3) How information leaks: insiders report intentions before official acts, with reporter-specific reliability and lag, while the contract requires the official act. (4) Selection among alternatives: a destination among 32 teams, which coach goes first among 32, or which games a network flexes. Probabilities come from calendar-structured hazards, competing-risk orderings, categorical choice models and reference-class base rates, with edge mostly in timing and in resolution wording.

stages.name: Event owner and decision process
stages.description: Each contract has a decision-maker: head-coach exits and hires are owner/GM decisions after performance and contract considerations; roster inclusion is a GM and coach decision under a 53-man limit; signings, extensions and trades are bilateral negotiations under the cap; retirement and supplemental-draft declaration are player decisions; primetime counts are league/broadcaster scheduling decisions. Identifying the decision-maker determines which information matters and what base rates apply, so the contract types cannot be pooled into one model.
stages.distribution: Mixture of categorical event types with distinct generators; very small samples per type (a handful of coach firings per year)

stages.name: Calendar structure and hazard timing
stages.description: Events concentrate in windows: coach firings in-season after bad losses and especially the week after the regular season; roster cuts on a fixed date; retirements after the season and before free agency; trade deadlines in early November (date taken from the original draft and not verified here; the league calendar varies by season); free agency opening in March and schedule release in May. A time-to-event model must therefore have a time-varying hazard that spikes at known dates and is near zero elsewhere, and a deadline in the contract (before Mar 1, 2027) integrates the hazard over those spikes.
stages.distribution: Piecewise-constant hazard with spikes at calendar dates; probability within a window is 1 - exp(-integral of hazard)

stages.name: Information flow from insiders to official act
stages.description: Credible insiders report agreements, intentions and injuries before the official act; the conversion probability depends on reporter tier, wording ('agreed to terms' vs 'expected to') and time to the announcement. The contract requires the official act, so the model must predict both occurrence and the lag against close time. Rumour mass without credible attribution has little value.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli conversion given a report; lag distribution is right-skewed (hours to weeks); high reporter heterogeneity

stages.name: Player movement: trade hazard, next-team choice and contract value
stages.description: KXNFLTRADE is a hazard of an officially processed trade before a date, concentrated before the early-November trade deadline (date from the original draft, unverified) and in the March-to-draft window; it rises with the team's record falling out of contention, the player's contract (cheap control is tradeable, dead cap blocks moves) and reported availability. KXNFLNEXTTEAM is a categorical choice over the current team (extension, franchise tag, simply remaining under contract), 31 other teams and 'Retires / No Team', driven by contract status, cap space by team, positional need and reported interest. KXNFLCONTRACTSIZE (title only) is a value distribution anchored on positional market comps scaled by cap growth.
stages.distribution: Trade: piecewise hazard with deadline spike, most players near zero; next team: categorical with a large mass on the current team; contract size: right-skewed value distribution around positional comps

stages.name: Roster-battle process for the 53-man list
stages.description: A player's chance of making the initial 53 is a function of draft capital, contracted money (dead-cap cost of cutting), preseason performance, depth at the position, special-teams value and injury status. The contract excludes IR/PUP/suspended players, so an injured star may resolve NO, and the 53-man list is a constrained selection (a fixed number of slots by position group).
stages.distribution: Binary with strongly informative covariates; most starters near one; borderline players in the 30-70% range; the IR exclusion creates a discrete state

stages.name: Settlement wording and novelty events
stages.description: Official announcement versus report, effective-date clauses for retirement, rescission-proof trade settlement, practice-squad exclusion and NO-on-postponement for game location decide the label. KXNFLCOMPETE (a celebrity must take a snap, preseason included) is a signing-then-activation chain with a tiny base rate; KXNFLHKANE is the same chain without the snap; KXNFLGAMELOCATION is venue-retention risk for an international game (security, weather, stadium readiness). These have no football-performance driver and rest on reference-class priors. Reference classes are now defined per series in nfl.offfield_base_rate: KXNFLHKANE and KXNFLCOMPETE use a cross-sport-athlete class (non-football athletes publicly linked to an NFL tryout or signing, outcome official signing or a recorded snap within the window), KXNFLGAMELOCATION uses the history of announced international regular-season games and whether each was played in the announced city. The ownership-stake (KXNFLOWNERSTAKE) and stadium-completion (KXNFLSTADIUM) series were re-filed by the final series assignment to OUT_OF_SCOPE (franchise_ownership_business, team_facilities) and are explicitly excluded from this archetype.
stages.distribution: Deterministic rule application; novelty events are Poisson or Bernoulli with reference-class base rates

stages.name: Draft family: supplemental-draft declaration and draft-capital context
stages.description: The draft-order mechanism for 'k-th quarterback drafted' contracts now belongs to the separate draft archetype that owns KXNFLDRAFTQB. What remains here is KXNFLSUPDRAFTPICK: whether a player declares for the supplemental draft, a rare eligibility-driven decision (lost college eligibility, academic or disciplinary status) settled on the league's announcement. The draft board and QB class model are kept as context for draft-related specials and for 53-man and first-start contracts that depend on draft capital, not as the primary source for a selection-order market.
stages.distribution: Rare binary declaration event with a very low base rate in recent seasons; announcement-dated

stages.name: Coaching carousel: next coach out and candidate hires
stages.description: KXNFLNEXTCOACHOUT asks which permanent head coach leaves first after issuance and before Feb 15, 2027: a competing-risk race in which coach i wins with probability integral of h_i(t) times the joint survival of all other coaches, so a coach with a modest hazard can still be unlikely to be first if a hotter seat exists elsewhere. Interim coaches are excluded. KXNFLHIRECOACH asks whether a named candidate is hired as a coach before a date: vacancies opened by exits, the candidate's interest in returning, his reputation and connections to owners/GMs with openings, and the breadth of 'a coach' (head coach versus coordinator or other leagues).
stages.distribution: Competing risks across 32 coaches with calendar spikes (in-season firings after losses, Black Monday); hire: product of vacancy count and candidate selection share, a small probability for most named candidates

stages.name: Schedule windows and weather delays for scheduled games
stages.description: KXNFLPRIMETIME counts a team's games in SNF, MNF, TNF windows plus Thanksgiving and Christmas, excluding the Wednesday opener; after schedule release the base count is fixed and only flex scheduling moves it, driven by team records and appeal in flex-eligible weeks. KXNFLDELAY asks whether a game has any official weather delay (pre-start or in-game): this is mostly lightning within the stadium radius (a 30-minute suspension per strike, as stated in the original draft; the league lightning rule is not verified here) at open-air venues, so roof type, month, kickoff hour and regional thunderstorm climatology dominate, and a fixed dome has near-zero risk.
stages.distribution: Primetime: base count plus a small number of Bernoulli flex events; delay: rare Bernoulli (near zero indoors, a few percent for early-season afternoon games in thunderstorm-prone regions)

talent_strength.note: Team performance relative to expectation feeds coach hazards and trade contention; player value anchors contract size.

opponent_matchup.note: No opposing unit or matchup exists in off-field outcomes; opponents matter only through standings, which are already represented by the season simulation and have no separate matchup channel.

role_personnel.note: Roster slots, guarantee structure, positional need and destination choice.

availability_news.note: Insider reports and injury news precede official acts.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach exit and hire processes (the coaching carousel) are themselves outcomes here; scheme does not enter otherwise.

environment.note: Weather-delay hazard from roof, climatology and thunderstorm forecasts; venue retention risk for international games remains base-rate only.

game_context_script.note: The events are not produced by game scripts; game state matters only through standings and in-season firings after specific losses, which the hazard model handles.

pace_volume.note: There is no opportunity count such as plays or possessions; the equivalent exposure is calendar time at risk, which is handled by the hazard calendar rather than a volume input.

efficiency_conversion.note: The analog of a conversion rate is the probability that a credible report converts into the official act, by reporter and event type.

distribution_variance.note: Rare-event base rates and competing-risk ordering for next-coach-out.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Calendar windows (deadline, Black Monday, flex weeks), contract years and contention status.

officiating_rules.note: League roster, designation, cap and trade-processing rules set what counts.

settlement_contract.note: Announced-versus-reported, effective dates, rescission-proof trade processing, residual strikes (Retires / No Team) and close times.

nfl.event_calendar_hazard.label: Calendar-structured hazard curve by event type
nfl.event_calendar_hazard.mechanism: Time-varying hazard of each event type (coach exit, retirement, signing, trade, cut) across the league calendar.
nfl.event_calendar_hazard.rationale: Contracts with fixed dates (before Mar 1, 2027) integrate the hazard over uneven time; ignoring the spikes (Black Monday, cut-down, deadline) misallocates probability across the window.
nfl.event_calendar_hazard.measurement: From the transaction wire and coach history 2000-2025, count events per calendar week by type; estimate piecewise-constant weekly hazard with Gamma-Poisson shrinkage (prior shape 2, rate 4 pseudo-team-years); condition on state (team win % bin, contract year remaining); compute P(event in [now, deadline]) = 1 - exp(-sum of hazard x exposure); as-of date.
free_sources: Pro Football Reference coaches and transactions (free_scrape)
raw_data: event log: date, team, person, type
team standing by week, contract status
nfl.event_calendar_hazard.why: The key quantity for any 'before date' contract; the existing base-rate input does not define the calendar structure.

nfl.insider_report_conversion.label: Insider report-to-official-announcement conversion and lag
nfl.insider_report_conversion.mechanism: Probability and delay with which a report by a given insider and wording is followed by the official act.
nfl.insider_report_conversion.rationale: Settlement requires the official act; report credibility and lag determine whether the event resolves before the market closes.
nfl.insider_report_conversion.measurement: Build a table of reports (reporter, timestamp, wording class: 'agreed', 'expected', 'discussing') for 2018-2025, link to the official action; estimate conversion rate and median lag by reporter tier and wording with beta prior (alpha=2, beta=2) shrinkage; as-of report timestamp; output P(official within horizon).
free_sources: X/Twitter and NFL Network archives (own_capture needed)
Pro Football Reference transactions for official dates
raw_data: report log: reporter, text, timestamp
official transaction dates
nfl.insider_report_conversion.why: Directly estimates how much a report should move probability and when; the existing input is only a generic news feed.

nfl.initial_roster_cut_model.label: Initial 53-man roster inclusion model
nfl.initial_roster_cut_model.mechanism: Probability that a player is on the initial 53-man active roster given draft round, guarantees, preseason usage, position depth and injury status.
nfl.initial_roster_cut_model.rationale: Inclusion is a constrained selection with an explicit IR/PUP exclusion; stars on IR resolve NO, while fringe players depend on dead-cap cost and roster composition.
nfl.initial_roster_cut_model.measurement: Logistic regression on 2010-2025 cut-down histories: draft round, years of service, fully-secured (non-releasable) salary share, dead-cap cost of release, preseason snaps share, position group count vs slot count, injury designation at cut-down (IR/PUP/NFI flags as hard exclusion), special-teams snaps; shrink by team random effect (k=5 players per team); as-of cut-down eve.
raw_data: roster status by week 1
contract guarantees
preseason snaps
injury status at cut
nfl.initial_roster_cut_model.why: Specific mechanism for roster contracts that no existing input defines.

nfl.coach_exit_hazard.label: Head-coach exit hazard (firing, resignation, pre-announced departure)
nfl.coach_exit_hazard.mechanism: Hazard of a head coach leaving or announcing departure as a function of record vs expectation, contract status, owner history and calendar.
nfl.coach_exit_hazard.rationale: The contract counts announced exits, so resignations, retirements and mutual parting count; the hazard rises sharply after the season and after specific loss patterns.
nfl.coach_exit_hazard.measurement: Cox or discrete-time logistic hazard with covariates: win% minus preseason expectation (using non-market expectation from ratings), consecutive losses, playoff outcome, years remaining on contract (0-1 vs more), tenure, owner's historical turnover, GM tenure, prior-season record; train on 2000-2025 coach-seasons (about 800); report weekly hazard in-season and post-season; as-of date.
raw_data: coach-season table with outcomes and exit dates
team records
contract years remaining (press)
preseason own rating
nfl.coach_exit_hazard.why: Defines the hazard model beyond a qualitative hot-seat signal.

nfl.vote_outcome_model.label: Vote-share model for awards and the Top 100 list
nfl.vote_outcome_model.mechanism: Winner or rank probability from candidate quality, narrative, previous votes, timing and electorate composition, aggregated through each award's actual ballot, which is a PARAMETER of the model per award and season: voters V, places K and points vector w. AP ballot parameters per award and season, each with its evidence status. (a) MVP, 2025 season: 50 voters, 5 places, points 10-5-3-2-1; seen in search-result copies of AP wire text, AP primary page not fetched. (b) MVP, 2023 season: 5 places, points 10-5-3-2-1 (a per-position tally such as 49-0-1-0-0=493 was seen in a search copy); primary not fetched. (c) The other seven AP awards, 2025 season: 5 places, points 10-5-3-2-1, 50-voter panel; seen in search-result copies of the AP finalist and results text, primary not fetched. (d) MVP from 2022 as a top-5 ballot with only the top three places for the other awards (5-3-1): reported in search copies of an AP statement, UNVERIFIED, and the season in which the non-MVP awards moved to five places is unknown. (e) Single first-place vote before 2022: UNVERIFIED. (f) Voter count for seasons other than 2025, the tie rule and the ballot close date: not found. (g) The tally Stafford 366 points / 24 firsts versus Maye 361 / 23 is reported in search copies as the 2025-season MVP result; the page date of one cited URL was ambiguous, so the season attribution is unconfirmed.
nfl.vote_outcome_model.rationale: Awards and ranks are decided by a small electorate with identifiable biases (position, team success, prior awards); the leader's share is concentrated.
nfl.vote_outcome_model.measurement: Per AP award, model each voter's ranked ballot: rank-ordered (exploded) logit of candidate placements on features (team win% at ballot close, statistical rank within position by EPA or season totals, prior award wins, position dummy), ridge penalty by leave-one-season-out CV, prior weight 3 pseudo-observations; fit seasons whose full AP placement counts are published, with K, V and w read per award and season from the ballot-parameter table in the mechanism (not hard-coded) and any single-vote seasons on first-place votes only as a separate regime sharing feature weights through a hierarchical prior. Simulate V ballots per draw (V=50 is seen in search copies for 2025 only) and score each with the points vector w of that award-season (10-5-3-2-1 seen in search copies for the MVP and, in 2025, the other AP awards; any other scheme is read from that season's AP tally), winner = highest points (ties shared). Non-AP processes (PFWA Executive of the Year, Hall of Fame, All-Pro, T100) keep their own model: T100 ordered logit on previous rank, change in production, position group, age. Output P(candidate=winner) and P(rank=r); group markets P(group) = sum of P(win) by team at announcement time with 1/N co-winner payout; Executive of the Year tie probability = own-award co-winner frequency shrunk to comparable awards with weight 10. As-of ballot close.
free_sources: Pro Football Reference awards and voting (free_scrape)
raw_data: historical winners and vote tallies, candidate stats, previous T100 ranks
nfl.vote_outcome_model.why: Kept for catalog traceability; award and Top 100 series are no longer filed in this archetype and this input is not staged here.

nfl.draft_qb_class_model.label: Draft positional-selection model (QB class order, draft order, team need and trade-up)
nfl.draft_qb_class_model.mechanism: The k-th quarterback drafted is determined by the ranked order in which teams on the clock select QBs, which depends on consensus prospect rank, the order of picks of QB-needy teams, and trades that move teams up.
nfl.draft_qb_class_model.rationale: Draft contracts such as 'player X is the 3rd quarterback drafted' are order statistics over a small class (about 8 to 14 QBs drafted per year), where a single early-round team's need and a trade-up change the rank of all later QBs. The generic consensus-board input gives one prospect's rank but not the joint ordering that the count-based contract settles on.
nfl.draft_qb_class_model.measurement: Plackett-Luce ordering model over the QBs in the class: utility_j = -beta*ln(consensus_rank_j) + gamma*need(team on the clock) with consensus_rank an average of at least 5 public big boards (time-stamped; weights proportional to each board's historical rank-correlation with actual draft order), beta and gamma fit by maximum likelihood on 2010-2025 drafts (about 180 QBs), team need = 1 if the current starter contract expires within one year or the starter's EPA per play is below the league 25th percentile; draft order from the final standings and traded picks. Simulate 20,000 drafts including a trade-up probability for QB-needy teams outside the top 5 (estimated from the 2010-2025 share of QBs taken before their consensus slot, shrunk with k=5). Report P(QB j is the k-th QB selected) and P(QB j drafted in the top n). As-of: refreshed after the combine, pro days, and each time a credible insider reports intentions; final run at draft start. Betting or market odds are excluded and used as benchmarks only.
free_sources: public big-board and mock draft aggregator pages
team standings and traded-pick lists (nflverse, league site)
raw_data: draft_picks: season, round, pick, team, player, position
time-stamped consensus big boards
team QB contract and starter EPA
nfl.draft_qb_class_model.why: Joint ordering model for quarterbacks in a draft class, kept as context because no draft-position series is filed here.

nfl.broadcast_role_assignment.label: Broadcast and event role assignment model (announced crews, contracts and appearance history)
nfl.broadcast_role_assignment.mechanism: A named person performs a role in a named network's broadcast only if the network assigns them to that event and they appear, which follows announced crew sheets, multi-year talent contracts and prior appearance frequency.
nfl.broadcast_role_assignment.rationale: KXNFLROLE settles on whether a person performs as an on-air analyst in a specific network broadcast in a window; this is a staffing decision with a mostly public paper trail (crew announcements, contract news), not an athletic outcome, and it needs base rates by role type rather than a vote or a season model.
nfl.broadcast_role_assignment.measurement: P(role) = P(person on the network's announced crew for at least one qualifying event in the window) x P(appears given assigned). Crew assignment is estimated by logistic regression on the person's number of qualifying events in each of the previous 3 seasons (with weights 0.5, 0.3, 0.2), contract end year, the network's announced lead-crew roster (binary), and whether the event is the network's lead broadcast; P(appears | assigned) = 1 minus the withdrawal rate (illness, conflicts) from the past 5 seasons, shrunk with k=10 events toward 0.97. As-of: each network crew press release and contract report, stamped to the hour; before an announcement the prior-season frequency is used.
free_sources: network press releases and crew announcements (free)
raw_data: network broadcast crew sheets by event and season
talent contract announcements with dates
nfl.broadcast_role_assignment.why: Kept for catalog traceability; the on-air role series is no longer filed in this archetype and this input is not staged here.

nfl.player_trade_hazard.label: Named-player trade hazard before a date
nfl.player_trade_hazard.mechanism: Probability that a named player is traded (officially processed) within a window, from team contention status, contract structure and reported availability.
nfl.player_trade_hazard.rationale: Trades cluster before the trade deadline and in the offseason; most players have near-zero hazard, so team context and contract terms (dead cap, years of control) separate candidates, and reports of shopping are the strongest signal.
nfl.player_trade_hazard.measurement: Discrete-time weekly logistic hazard trained on 2010-2025 player-weeks: covariates = team win% minus preseason model expectation, weeks to trade deadline (indicator of final 2 weeks), dead cap if traded / cap hit, years of control remaining, age, positional value tier, credible-report flag (from nfl.insider_report_conversion); P(trade before date) = 1 - prod(1 - h_w) over weeks to the date; base-rate shrinkage toward position-season frequency with k=500 player-seasons; as-of each week.
raw_data: transactions: date, player_id, from_team, to_team, type
contracts: cap hit, dead cap by year, years remaining
standings by week
nfl.player_trade_hazard.why: KXNFLTRADE settles on an officially processed trade before a date.

nfl.player_destination_choice.label: Next-team categorical choice for a named player (incl. current team and retire/no team)
nfl.player_destination_choice.mechanism: Distribution over the player's team on a date: remain with current team, each other team, or retire/unsigned, from contract status, team cap space and positional need.
nfl.player_destination_choice.rationale: Next-team markets list every candidate team plus the current team and a residual; the current team often carries most mass (contract, tag, extension), and other teams are ranked by cap space, need and reported interest, not by quality alone.
nfl.player_destination_choice.measurement: Stage 1: P(move) = logistic on 2012-2025 veteran offseasons (contract expired or released) with features years remaining, franchise-tag eligibility flag, age, prior-season snap share, retirement-eligible age; ridge lambda by CV. Stage 2: conditional multinomial logit over 31 other teams with features (i) team cap space on the as-of date from a dated OTC snapshot, (ii) starter gap = team's best current starter's EPA-or-grade percentile at the player's position minus the player's, floored at 0, (iii) draft capital spent at the position in the last 2 drafts, (iv) 1[head coach or coordinator previously coached player], (v) 1[prior-team-of-record tie]; drop the subjective 'reported interest' flag unless captured with timestamp (own_capture). P(retire/no team) from age-position base rate. Shrink utilities with Dirichlet alpha=1. As-of timestamped snapshot before the decision window.
raw_data: team cap space by date (vintage snapshots)
player contract status and tags
depth charts / starter value by position
transactions history
nfl.player_destination_choice.why: KXNFLNEXTTEAM resolves on which team the player is with (or retired/unsigned) by the date.

nfl.contract_value_comps.label: Positional contract value comps scaled by cap growth
nfl.contract_value_comps.mechanism: Expected new-contract value (APY and total) for a player from recent comparable contracts at the position, scaled to the projected salary cap.
nfl.contract_value_comps.rationale: Next-contract-size markets depend on how the market for the position has moved; the most recent top contract at the position resets the scale and cap growth shifts all values, while age and injury discount it.
nfl.contract_value_comps.measurement: For position p, take contracts signed in the last 24 months, express APY as % of the cap in the signing year; fit a quantile regression of APY%cap on player value (prior 2-season EPA or PFF-free equivalent production metrics), age and contract-year status; predicted APY = quantiles x projected cap of the signing year; report the distribution of total value = APY x expected years; as-of market time.
raw_data: contracts: player, position, sign date, years, total, APY, guarantees
salary cap by year
player production stats
nfl.contract_value_comps.why: KXNFLCONTRACTSIZE (title only) settles on the size of a player's next contract.

nfl.coach_exit_competing_order.label: Competing-risk probability that a named coach is the next head coach out
nfl.coach_exit_competing_order.mechanism: Probability that coach i's departure occurs before every other permanent head coach's, from all 32 coaches' time-varying exit hazards.
nfl.coach_exit_competing_order.rationale: Next-coach-out pays on order, not occurrence: a coach's chance of being first depends on how hot the other seats are and on when each hazard spikes (in-season vs Black Monday), so per-coach probabilities from nfl.coach_exit_hazard must be combined in a competing-risk calculation.
nfl.coach_exit_competing_order.measurement: Using weekly hazards h_j(t) from nfl.coach_exit_hazard for all 32 coaches from issuance to Feb 15, 2027, compute P(i first) = sum_t h_i(t) prod_j S_j(t-1) prod_{j!=i}(1-h_j(t)) with simultaneous Black Monday exits split by announcement timestamp order (empirical tie-break by time of announcement); residual 'none before deadline' = prod_j S_j(T); recompute weekly as standings update.
raw_data: weekly coach hazards for all 32 teams
coach exit announcement timestamps
nfl.coach_exit_competing_order.why: KXNFLNEXTCOACHOUT is a race among all head coaches.

nfl.coach_candidate_hire_model.label: Named-candidate coaching hire probability
nfl.coach_candidate_hire_model.mechanism: Probability that a named candidate is hired as a coach before a date, from the number of expected vacancies, the candidate's profile and interest, and ties to decision-makers with openings.
nfl.coach_candidate_hire_model.rationale: Hire markets depend first on how many jobs open (from exit hazards) and then on candidate share; former head coaches returning, coordinators and media figures have very different conversion rates, and reported interviews are the strongest signal.
nfl.coach_candidate_hire_model.measurement: Expected vacancies V = sum of exit probabilities from nfl.coach_exit_hazard before the date (plus coordinator openings if the contract counts them); candidate share from a conditional logit over 2005-2025 hiring cycles with features: prior head-coach experience and record, years out of coaching, current role, age, number of reported interviews, prior ties to the hiring GM/owner; P(hire) = 1 - exp(-V x share); as-of market time.
raw_data: coach hiring history by cycle
candidate interview reports with timestamps
exit hazards
nfl.coach_candidate_hire_model.why: KXNFLHIRECOACH settles on a named person being hired as a coach.

nfl.weather_delay_hazard.label: Game weather-delay hazard (lightning and severe weather)
nfl.weather_delay_hazard.mechanism: Probability of any official weather delay (pre-start or in-game) for a scheduled game, from roof type, location climatology, month, kickoff hour and the thunderstorm forecast.
nfl.weather_delay_hazard.rationale: Weather delays are almost always lightning within the stadium's radius at open-air venues in early-season afternoon or evening games; fixed domes are near zero and retractable roofs depend on roof policy, so a generic weather input does not capture the event.
nfl.weather_delay_hazard.measurement: Logistic model on 2010-2025 games (outcome: any weather delay from game books/news): features = roof (open/retractable/dome), month, kickoff local hour, regional climatological thunderstorm-day frequency for the month (NOAA), and at forecast time the NWS thunderstorm probability for the kickoff window +/- 3 hours; shrink venue effects toward roof-type means with k=40 games; as-of the 24h and 3h forecast vintages.
raw_data: schedules: game_id, stadium, roof, kickoff time
weather delay records per game
NWS thunderstorm probability forecasts by location and hour
NOAA monthly thunderstorm-day climatology
nfl.weather_delay_hazard.why: KXNFLDELAY resolves on any official weather delay of a game.

interactions.mechanism: A report from a top-tier insider with 'agreed to terms' wording converts to an official signing with high probability within days, while a speculative report by a lesser source barely moves the hazard; the update depends on reporter tier, wording and time before market close.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare event frequencies after reports binned by reporter tier and wording class.

interactions.mechanism: A losing team with an owner who has a history of quick firings and a coach with an expiring contract has a firing hazard that multiplies these factors, especially after the season ends; no single factor is sufficient in isolation.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the discrete-time hazard with interactions of win% shortfall, contract years and owner history.

interactions.mechanism: A player with large contracted money is nearly sure to make the 53 unless on IR; a fringe player with no guarantee has probability set by roster slots at his position; the IR designation at cut-down switches the outcome to NO regardless of talent.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate inclusion by guarantee tercile with and without injury exclusion flag.

interactions.mechanism: The coach-out hazard is near zero between weeks, climbs slowly in the season after bad losses and jumps after the final game; a date-based contract's probability depends mainly on whether the horizon spans the post-season window.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare empirical hazard by calendar week against a constant-hazard model.

interactions.mechanism: A player's trade hazard rises sharply only when his team falls out of contention in the weeks right before the trade deadline; a contender's veteran or a team still in the race has near-zero deadline hazard, so contention status gates the calendar spike.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit weekly trade hazards with an interaction between playoff probability (from standings simulation) and weeks-to-deadline on 2010-2025 player-weeks and compare with an additive model.

interactions.mechanism: Delay risk is essentially zero under a fixed roof and becomes material only at open-air venues once the forecast thunderstorm probability in the kickoff window passes a threshold, because the league's lightning rule suspends play for any strike within the stadium radius.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot delay frequency against forecast thunderstorm probability split by roof type on 2010-2025 games and test for a kink versus a linear logistic fit.

nonlinearities.why: The hazard is piecewise: Black Monday, cut-down day, trade deadline, free agency and flex-announcement dates carry most of the mass, so a smooth time-to-event model misallocates probability across weeks.

nonlinearities.shape: logistic in draft round with hard exclusion
nonlinearities.why: Inclusion probability falls steeply from first-round picks to undrafted free agents, and an IR placement acts as a hard zero rather than a smooth penalty.

A coach's probability of being next out is a steeply convex function of his hazard relative to the hottest other seats: doubling a mid-ranked coach's hazard barely moves his first-out probability while the top seat holds most of the mass.

contract.settlement_definition: Eight live series; seven have rules text, KXNFLWEEKSTART is TITLE_ONLY. Participation: KXNFLWEEKCOMPETE resolves YES if the named player takes at least one snap, even if nullified by penalty, in the stated regular-season week; KXNFLEVERYWEEKCOMPETE needs at least one snap in every regular-season game played by the team whose active roster he is on, byes excluded and games before he joins a team not counting; KXNFLRETURN needs him to enter a regular-season game for the named team after a date and before a week (preseason excluded). Depth chart: KXNFLFIRSTSTART (listed as starting QB 'for the first time this season') and KXNFLDEBUT ('for the first time', i.e. a career first start) resolve YES on his team's official depth chart within an inclusive week range (byes skipped; fallback to official team communications); KXNFLWEEKQBSTART resolves for the QB listed as the team's starter in the stated week; KXNFLDEPTHPOSITIONCLEQB2 resolves YES if the player is officially designated QB2 for the week (injured-but-listed counts; practice-squad/inactive players do not qualify unless promoted; elimination before a postseason week resolves NO; bye weeks use the last chart before the bye). Source: official depth charts/team communications for designations; official participation records for snaps.

variants_and_edge_cases: Five availability definitions: one snap in a week (WEEKCOMPETE), a snap in every team game of the season (EVERYWEEKCOMPETE), first regular-season appearance for a named team in a window (RETURN), depth-chart starter (FIRSTSTART, DEBUT, WEEKQBSTART, WEEKSTART title only) and depth-chart QB2 (DEPTHPOSITION).

Depth-chart contracts settle on the published listing: a listed starter who is then inactive still resolves YES, an injured but listed QB2 resolves YES, and a surprise starter after a late injury may not appear on a chart published earlier in the week.

KXNFLDEBUT's sampled market uses first-start wording without 'this season' (a career first start, week range 7-10 for a rookie QB), whereas KXNFLFIRSTSTART is the first start of the current season; neither is a first-appearance definition despite the DEBUT title.

EVERYWEEKCOMPETE: byes excluded and games before joining a roster do not count; whether a week in which the player is on a reserve list (IR, suspension) breaks the streak follows from 'each game ... played by a team on whose active roster' he is a member, which suggests games while off the active roster do not count against him (not explicit).
QB2 postseason weeks resolve NO if the team is already eliminated; bye weeks use the last chart before the bye.
KXNFLNEXTTEAM was re-filed to off_field_events and is no longer claimed here.

QB2 text says an injured player still listed at the position resolves YES but also that inactive players do not qualify unless promoted to the active roster; precedence for an injured, listed but game-day-inactive QB2 is not stated.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official depth charts published by the team and official team communications (injury reports, press releases) for designations; official game participation records/play-by-play for snaps.

mechanism.summary: Availability outcomes come from a sequence of decisions by medical staff, coaches and front offices acting on physical state and incentives. For a one-snap participation market: P(plays) = P(medically able on game day) x P(team chooses to activate him) x P(he takes at least one snap given active). Medical ability follows an injury-specific recovery clock (a hamstring strain, a high ankle sprain and an ACL tear have very different return-time distributions) revealed through the practice sequence (did not participate, limited, full) and the Friday designation; the team's choice reflects stakes, rest policy for veterans, roster depth and sometimes a coach's reluctance to disclose; and the snap condition fails for emergency depth players and gadget roles. For first-start markets the process is a hazard over weeks that the current starter is replaced (benching for performance, injury, a bye-week reset, a contract or draft-capital decision) and the depth chart lists the new name; the chart is a team publication with its own timing. Weekly starter and QB2 markets read the same depth-chart process as a categorical over the team's quarterbacks each week, and the every-week participation market compounds a weekly injury and rest hazard over a whole season. Close time determines which of these signals have been revealed.

stages.name: Physical state and injury recovery clock
stages.description: The underlying cause is the injury (or absence of one): body part, grade, whether surgery occurred, and elapsed days since onset. Each injury type has a recovery-time distribution that is right-skewed with a long tail of setbacks, and return-to-play rules (IR minimum of four games, designated-to-return windows) put hard constraints on the clock. The player's own history of reinjury adds to the hazard.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed recovery time (Weibull/lognormal) by injury type; long tail of setbacks; discrete hard constraints from IR rules

stages.name: Practice sequence to official designation
stages.description: Between Wednesday and Friday, teams report each player's practice participation (did not participate, limited, full) and then a game designation (Out, Doubtful, Questionable). The mapping from the sequence to actual participation is calibratable and differs by position and by team transparency: a limited-limited-full pattern for a skill player implies something different from the same pattern for a lineman, and a Friday 'Questionable' resolves very differently across teams.
stages.distribution: Ordinal sequence mapped to Bernoulli participation; step probabilities at designations (Out ~ 0, Doubtful low, Questionable around half, no designation near one)

stages.name: Team decision, rest policy and healthy scratches
stages.description: Even a healthy player can be inactive: veterans rested in meaningless late games, rookies and depth players left off the 46-man game-day list, players disciplined by coaches or held back after returning. The decision depends on coach, roster composition, the stakes (clinched seeds) and the opponent.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli at the team's discretion; base rates by role and coach; higher for veterans in weeks 17-18 and for backups

stages.name: Depth-chart ordering and QB-change hazard
stages.description: For first-start contracts the question is whether and when the depth chart lists the player first. A QB gets promoted when the incumbent is injured, benched (performance relative to expectation, team record, a bye week as a natural reset point) or when development timelines force a change. The hazard per week depends on incumbent performance, the challenger's draft capital and contract, and the coach's patience; the contract's window turns this into a probability over about 3-4 charts. The incumbent-versus-challenger gap is measured by nfl.qb_challenger_prior, which uses a draft-slot prior when the challenger has few dropbacks.
stages.distribution: Discrete-time hazard per published chart; event probability 1 - product of (1 - h_week); rare but front-loaded after bye weeks

stages.name: Snap appearance given active
stages.description: A player who is active may not see a snap: an emergency third QB, a gadget wide receiver, a backup lineman, or a rotational back in a blowout. Whether special-teams snaps count is a contract detail. The conditional probability of at least one snap depends on role, game script and injury attrition among starters.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli with role-specific base rates; near one for starters and near zero for emergency depth

stages.name: Information vintage and market close
stages.description: The state of information available at market close is what matters: probability before Wednesday reflects only the injury and base rates; after Friday designations it reflects the practice sequence; after the 90-minute inactive list it is nearly decided. Contracts that close earlier carry a mixture over scenarios; those closing at kickoff are almost certain.
stages.distribution: Probability mass moves from a prior mixture to near 0/1 as vintages accrue; discrete jumps at report times

stages.name: Roster-status transitions for non-roster players
stages.description: For a retired, unsigned, suspended or long-term injured player the chain is not injury then designation then inactive list but a status transition: a decision to un-retire or sign, a contract before the roster deadline, a physical and activation (or IR/PUP activation), and then a snap. The sampled KXNFLWEEKCOMPETE subject is outside any current roster, and KXNFLRETURN requires a regular-season appearance for a named team before a given week, so probabilities come from comeback reference classes, activation-window rules and insider-reported interest rather than practice participation.
stages.distribution: Rare-event discrete-time hazards with long periods of near-zero probability and jumps at reported interest; binary outcomes after a multi-step funnel

stages.name: Weekly depth-chart slot designation: starter and QB2
stages.description: KXNFLWEEKQBSTART is a categorical over the team's quarterbacks for one week's published chart, and KXNFLDEPTHPOSITIONCLEQB2 asks who is listed second. The QB2 slot depends on the QB1 outcome: if the incumbent is injured or benched, the former QB2 moves up and a third QB (or a signing) becomes QB2, so P(player is QB2) = P(he is not promoted to QB1) x P(he outranks the remaining backups). Preseason competition, draft capital, coach statements and whether the team lists co-starters ('OR') decide the order; injured-but-listed players still count, so the chart publication policy matters more than health.
stages.distribution: Categorical over 2-4 quarterbacks per team-week; strong persistence week to week with jumps after injuries, bye weeks and benchings

stages.name: Season-long every-week participation streak
stages.description: KXNFLEVERYWEEKCOMPETE needs a snap in each of roughly 17 team games. The probability is a product of weekly survival terms: each week the player can miss through new injury (position- and age-specific weekly hazard, higher for players with a recent injury history), lingering injury (recovery clock), rest decisions late in the season and benching or healthy scratch. Because one miss ends the streak, small weekly hazards compound: a 3% weekly miss rate gives about 60% survival over 17 games. Trades do not break it, and games before he joins a roster do not count.
stages.distribution: Product of weekly Bernoulli survival terms with heterogeneous, positively autocorrelated hazards (injury begets missed games); strongly convex in the weekly hazard

nfl.injury_return_timeline.label: Injury-specific return-time distribution
nfl.injury_return_timeline.mechanism: Time from injury onset to first game played, by body part and severity.
nfl.injury_return_timeline.rationale: Whether a player appears in week k depends on the recovery clock; type-specific survival curves replace an undifferentiated 'injured' flag.
nfl.injury_return_timeline.measurement: Define onset as the first weekly injury report listing the player with a given report_primary_injury; time-to-event = number of team games missed before the first game with snaps >0, censored at season end. Fit a Weibull (or Kaplan-Meier where n>=30) per body-part group (knee, ankle, hamstring, shoulder, concussion, other) and position group using 2009-2025 nflverse injuries and snap counts, stratified by first-report status (Out/Doubtful/Questionable) instead of surgery, which is unobserved. Shrink each stratum curve to the position-pooled curve with k=10 cases. Output P(returns by game k) as-of the report date.
raw_data: injury reports by week: body part, status, practice, games missed after onset
nfl.injury_return_timeline.why: A recovery clock is the mechanism of return markets; the existing list records status snapshots without a time-to-return model.

nfl.designation_to_play_calibration.label: Practice-sequence and designation to play-probability calibration
nfl.designation_to_play_calibration.mechanism: Calibrated P(plays | Wednesday, Thursday, Friday practice status, designation, position, team, week).
nfl.designation_to_play_calibration.rationale: The mapping is team-specific: some teams use Questionable for near-certain players, others reserve it for coin flips; position matters because linemen and skill players differ.
nfl.designation_to_play_calibration.measurement: Hierarchical logistic regression of played (>=1 snap) on practice-sequence pattern (e.g., DNP-LP-FP), designation, position group, days of rest, and team random effect with shrinkage prior (tau fitted); training 2012-2025 injury reports with vintages; as-of each report time; output P(play) with credible interval.
free_sources: nflverse injuries (practice status, report status) and snap counts
NFL official injury reports (own_capture for timing)
raw_data: injury reports with practice status per day, designations, outcome snaps
nfl.designation_to_play_calibration.why: Existing inputs hold the raw data but no calibration of participation by sequence and team.

nfl.healthy_inactive_base_rate.label: Healthy-inactive and rest base rates by role and coach
nfl.healthy_inactive_base_rate.mechanism: Probability that a healthy player is inactive due to coach choice (rest, discipline, 46-man cut).
nfl.healthy_inactive_base_rate.rationale: About a fifth of inactives are healthy; rest decisions are concentrated in weeks 17-18 and for veterans on clinched teams.
nfl.healthy_inactive_base_rate.measurement: From inactive lists and injury report absences (no injury listed) 2015-2025: rate by position, age band, depth slot, team clinch status, coach; shrink to league by k=15 player-games; as-of the week.
raw_data: inactive list, injury report, snap counts
nfl.healthy_inactive_base_rate.why: Handles the absences with no injury, which injury inputs cannot predict.

nfl.qb_change_hazard.label: Starting-QB change hazard (benching or promotion) by week
nfl.qb_change_hazard.mechanism: Per-week hazard that the depth chart lists a different starting QB than the previous week.
nfl.qb_change_hazard.rationale: First-start contracts are about the hazard of leaving the starter's role; incumbent performance, team record and the next QB's draft capital govern it, and the weeks right after the bye are higher hazard.
nfl.qb_change_hazard.measurement: Event = a different QB is the week's starter for a non-injury reason (exclude injury inactives and rest weeks). Discrete-time logistic over team-weeks 2010-2025 with features: incumbent EPA/dropback over last 6 games minus nfl.qb_efficiency prior (z), incumbent turnovers per game last 4, team win% minus own-model expectation, weeks since bye, backup draft round (1, 2-3, 4+, UDFA), incumbent contracted-money flag (OTC), head-coach tenure in years; drop the unobservable 'owner pressure'. Ridge penalty by leave-one-season-out CV. Output weekly hazard h_w and cumulative 1 - prod(1-h_w) over scheduled non-bye weeks in the horizon. As-of report date.
raw_data: QB-week table: starter id, performance, record, depth chart, bye
draft round/contract of backup
coach tenure
nfl.qb_change_hazard.why: The key mechanism for first-start contracts, absent from the existing list.

nfl.snap_appearance_given_active.label: P(at least one snap | active) by role
nfl.snap_appearance_given_active.mechanism: Probability that an active player plays at least one snap (including or excluding special teams) by depth slot and script.
nfl.snap_appearance_given_active.rationale: The contract requires a snap, so an active emergency QB or deep rotation player may resolve NO; the base rate varies by role.
nfl.snap_appearance_given_active.measurement: From snap counts 2016-2025: fraction of active player-games with at least one offensive, defensive or special-teams snap by position and depth slot; shrinkage k=10 games; adjust for spread (blowouts raise backup snaps); output separate probabilities with and without special-teams snaps.
raw_data: snap counts per player-game by unit (off, def, ST)
nfl.snap_appearance_given_active.why: Settlement requires a snap rather than active status. Its catalog measurement adjusts for the spread; here blowout exposure comes from the market-free nfl.model_margin_lattice.

nfl.depth_chart_publication_lag.label: Depth-chart publication mechanics and lag by team
nfl.depth_chart_publication_lag.mechanism: How and when each team publishes its official depth chart and how 'starter' is encoded.
nfl.depth_chart_publication_lag.rationale: First-start contracts settle on the published chart; teams differ on publication day and encoding (or-designations), so the label can differ from who actually starts.
nfl.depth_chart_publication_lag.measurement: Per team-week from archive of depth charts (team websites and nflverse depth_charts), record publication weekday, whether an 'or' slot is used, change relative to prior week; compute P(chart lists a different QB1 than the actual week's starter); as-of week.
raw_data: depth chart snapshots with timestamp
nfl.depth_chart_publication_lag.why: Settlement artefact separate from football events.

nfl.roster_designation_constraints.label: Roster designation and league-rule hard constraints (IR, PUP, NFI, suspension)
nfl.roster_designation_constraints.mechanism: Mandatory minimum absence lengths and eligibility windows from the IR, PUP, NFI and suspension rules.
nfl.roster_designation_constraints.rationale: A player on IR cannot return for four games; suspensions have fixed lengths; these hard constraints dominate the injury recovery curve in the short run.
nfl.roster_designation_constraints.measurement: Rule table by season (IR minimum games, designated-to-return count, practice window 21 days, PUP and NFI rules, suspension length) joined to the player's status on each date; output earliest eligible game and the probability mass allowed by rule; as-of transaction wire.
raw_data: roster status by date, rules by season
nfl.roster_designation_constraints.why: Hard rules truncate the distribution of return dates and are missing from the existing list.

nfl.non_roster_return_status.label: Non-roster status transition model (retired, free agent, suspended or unsigned player returning to play)
nfl.non_roster_return_status.mechanism: A player who is not on an active roster can only take a snap after a chain of discrete events: ending retirement or suspension, signing with a team, passing a physical, and being activated, each with its own timing and decision-maker.
nfl.non_roster_return_status.rationale: The injury-report-to-inactive-list mechanism does not apply to a retired or unsigned player such as the sampled KXNFLWEEKCOMPETE subject (a player outside any current roster); the live contracts KXNFLRETURN and KXNFLNEXTTEAM are also status-transition events, so a separate model with reference classes for comebacks is required.
nfl.non_roster_return_status.measurement: P(plays in week w) = P(contract signed by the week-w roster deadline) x P(activated and takes a snap | signed). Estimate the first factor as a discrete-time hazard on retired and unsigned veterans 2000-2025 (age, years since last game, Pro Bowl count, stated intent in the previous 12 months as a binary flag, team contract interest reported by named insiders as a binary flag with a timestamp, days to the target week), with ridge shrinkage and a Beta(1, 19) prior for the base comeback rate; estimate the second from signing-to-first-snap lags of mid-season veteran signings (median lag in weeks, shrunk with k=8 signings). For NEXTTEAM contracts output P(team k) by multinomial logit on prior-team cap space, position need and reported interest, with a 'retires or no team' category. As-of: each transaction-wire timestamp and insider report time.
free_sources: league transactions page and Pro-Football-Reference transactions (free_scrape)
raw_data: transaction wire
player status history
insider report log
nfl.non_roster_return_status.why: Covers WEEKCOMPETE for retired or unsigned players and RETURN (regular-season appearance for a named team in a window), which the injury-report chain cannot model. The NEXTTEAM clause in its catalog text is stale here (that series moved to off_field_events) and is not used.

nfl.qb_challenger_prior.label: Incumbent-versus-challenger quarterback value gap (draft-capital prior for unproven QBs)
nfl.qb_challenger_prior.mechanism: The expected performance gap between the incumbent starter and a challenger drives benching and promotion decisions; for rookies and players with few dropbacks the challenger's value rests on a prior built from draft position.
nfl.qb_challenger_prior.rationale: The first-start contracts (KXNFLFIRSTSTART, KXNFLDEBUT) are about a named unproven QB overtaking an incumbent, and the incumbent's in-season EPA alone ignores how good the challenger is expected to be; teams that spent a high pick tolerate a shorter leash for the incumbent.
nfl.qb_challenger_prior.measurement: gap_w = EPA_incumbent_w - EPA_challenger_prior_w where EPA_incumbent_w is the incumbent's opponent-adjusted EPA per dropback over the last 8 games with a prior of league-average QB EPA at weight 150 dropbacks, and EPA_challenger_prior_w = a regression of first-3-season EPA per dropback on log draft pick (2000-2025 QBs with at least 150 dropbacks) blended with the challenger's own preseason and in-game dropbacks using weight n/(n+150). Pick number enters as a continuous slope, undrafted as pick 260. Output the gap and its SD for the discrete-time logistic hazard in nfl.qb_change_hazard. As-of: after each game, with bye weeks excluded from the exposure count.
raw_data: pbp: passer id, epa, qb_dropback, week
draft_picks: player, pick, position
nfl.qb_challenger_prior.why: Defines the measurable QB gap the benching hazard needs, including for rookies with no NFL sample.

nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model.label: Weekly QB depth-chart slot probabilities (QB1, QB2) per team
nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model.mechanism: Probability that each of a team's quarterbacks is listed QB1 or QB2 on the week's official depth chart, propagating QB1 changes down the chart.
nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model.rationale: Starter and backup designation markets are coupled: a QB1 change promotes the QB2 and opens the QB2 slot, and teams differ in chart policy (co-starters, injured players kept listed), so a slot-level model is needed rather than a starter hazard alone.
nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model.measurement: For each team-week, start from the previous chart order; apply P(QB1 changes) from nfl.qb_change_hazard and injury status; conditional on a change, assign the new QB1 by challenger rank (nfl.qb_challenger_prior); QB2 = highest-ranked remaining QB with rank score from draft capital, preseason snaps with the first and second team, contract APY and coach statements (logit fit on 2016-2025 chart snapshots); injured-but-listed retained per team policy (team fixed effect for keeping injured QBs listed, shrunk k=20 weeks); as-of the latest published chart before close.
raw_data: depth chart snapshots: team, week, position, depth order, player_id, publication date
preseason snap counts by quarter
QB draft slot and contract APY
nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model.why: Prices KXNFLWEEKQBSTART and KXNFLDEPTHPOSITIONCLEQB2, which settle on chart slots rather than on play.

nfl.season_participation_streak_hazard.label: Weekly miss hazard compounded over a season (every-week participation)
nfl.season_participation_streak_hazard.mechanism: Probability that a player takes a snap in every team game of a season, from a weekly hazard of missing a game through injury, rest or benching.
nfl.season_participation_streak_hazard.rationale: Every-week participation is a long product of weekly survivals; a weekly miss rate that looks small compounds to large season-level failure probability, and missed games cluster after injuries, so independence understates the streak's survival among durable players and overstates it for injury-prone ones.
nfl.season_participation_streak_hazard.measurement: Discrete-time logistic hazard of missing week w given active-roster membership, trained on 2012-2025 player-weeks: covariates = position, age, prior-season games missed, current injury designation, snaps per game (exposure), week >= 17 x team clinched flag; include a frailty term (player random effect, shrinkage from 3 prior seasons); P(streak) = prod_w (1 - h_w) over remaining scheduled games via simulation that carries injury state forward; as-of market time.

interactions.mechanism: The same practice pattern (limited, limited, full) predicts play at different rates for different positions and teams: for offensive linemen and QBs the full Friday practice often means active, while for running backs a limited Friday after a lower-body injury means a smaller snap load but still a play; the mapping is conditional on position and team transparency.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(play) by pattern within position group and team tercile and compare with pooled estimate.

interactions.mechanism: Return probability is zero until the IR minimum has passed, then follows the injury-specific clock, and a coach's statement about 'week to week' shifts the clock; the curve is piecewise, with a hard step at four games for players on IR.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare empirical return week to IR minimum and injury type for players placed on IR.

interactions.mechanism: QB benching hazard is low during the season and rises in the week after a bye or a bad loss; the chart for that week is the first moment the change is visible, so the contract window determines whether the hazard spike falls inside it.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate hazard by weeks since bye and by prior game result; map to windows 7-10.

interactions.mechanism: A Questionable veteran on a team that has clinched is much more likely to be held out than the same player on a team fighting for a seed; stakes change the mapping from designation to play, mainly in the last two weeks.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare play rates for Questionable players by clinch status and week.

interactions.mechanism: For a market that closes before the inactive list, probability is a mixture over states; after the list the outcome is nearly known, so time-to-close determines how much information the pregame model can use and where stale quotes appear.
interactions.how_to_test: Measure forecast accuracy by hours-to-kickoff at close.

interactions.mechanism: The QB2 slot probability depends on the QB1 outcome: when the incumbent is healthy and performing, the backup order is stable and QB2 markets are near-deterministic; once a QB1 change becomes likely, the current QB2 is likely to be promoted out of the QB2 slot, so P(QB2) falls as P(QB1 change) rises for the current backup and rises for the third-stringer.
interactions.how_to_test: On 2016-2025 chart snapshots, regress next-week QB2 identity on current QB2 and an indicator of a QB1 change, and compare slot transition matrices with and without a QB1 change.

nonlinearities.why: Participation probability steps from about zero (Out) through low (Doubtful) and roughly even (Questionable) to near one (no designation), so treating designation as ordinal-linear misstates the middle category.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in performance shortfall and spike after bye
nonlinearities.why: Benching probability is low until performance falls below a threshold, then rises quickly; and the week after the bye has a spike, so a linear performance coefficient misses the clustering.

nonlinearities.shape: right-skewed survival with hard step at the IR minimum
nonlinearities.why: Return time has a long tail of setbacks and a hard floor for IR placements; the probability of playing by week k is not linear in elapsed time.

Season streak survival is approximately exp(-17h): moving the weekly miss hazard from 1% to 4% drops survival from about 84% to about 50%, so small errors in weekly hazard become large errors in price.

contract.settlement_definition: Four live series; three have rules text (KXNFLPASSTDS, KXNFLPASSTDSPROT, KXNFLPASSINT), KXNFLCAREERPASSTDS is TITLE_ONLY. Single-game count markets resolve YES if the named QB records at least N passing touchdowns or N passing interceptions (floor_strike 3.5 = '4+' TDs, 2.5 = '3+' INTs, strike_type greater). If he is active but does not appear in any live play the market settles to the fair market price before game start; once he appears in one live play, even one nullified by penalty, it settles on the recorded statistic. KXNFLPASSTDSPROT additionally settles at the pre-kickoff fair price if the QB plays in the first half but in no play after it (including overtime), unless he already reached the count. No sampled text states whether overtime statistics count for the standard props, or the stat-correction window; source is the official game statistics. The career series' counting window and strike construction are not visible.

variants_and_edge_cases: Strike construction: floor_strike 3.5 ('4+') for TDs and 2.5 ('3+') for interceptions on integer counts; rungs are nested P(>=1) >= P(>=2) >= ... and a ladder must be monotone; no push.

Standard versus protected TD contracts differ for a QB pulled in a blowout or injured at halftime: standard markets stay live with a truncated count; protected markets void to a pre-kickoff fair price unless the count is already reached. No protected interception series is live.

Interceptions count as official interceptions thrown (pick-sixes included); a nullified play counts only for participation ('even if nullified by penalty'), while the counted statistic follows the official stat sheet.
Overtime statistics are not mentioned for the standard props; protected text mentions overtime only for the participation test.
KXNFLCAREERPASSTDS (title only) is a career milestone accrual over remaining seasons; the season passing-TD, completions and attempts series are no longer filed here and are not claimed.

mechanism.summary: A quarterback's touchdown-pass count is a thinned counting process: attempts times the per-attempt TD probability, where attempts are set by the team's pass volume (game script, pace, pass rate over expected) and the QB's playing time, and the per-attempt TD probability is concentrated in a few attempts inside the 20 and especially the 5-yard line. Therefore the number of goal-to-go and red-zone dropbacks is the key opportunity variable, and the pass-versus-run split near the goal line (the QB's rushing and the goal-line back) determines how many of the team's TDs are passes. Interceptions are a separate thinned process: attempts times the per-attempt interception rate, which is a mixture of bad decisions (turnover-worthy throws), pressure-induced errors, deep targeting and defender skill and randomness (tipped balls, drops by receivers). Both counts are overdispersed relative to Poisson because attempts, script and offensive environment are shared across the game. The quarterback must also play: active-but-no-play voids, protected markets void at a halftime pull, and blowout benching truncates attempts. The career version adds games played, retirement hazard and aging.

stages.name: Participation, protection and blowout pull
stages.description: The count only accumulates while the QB is in the game. Starter status, in-game injury and the coach's willingness to pull a starter in a lopsided score (typically when a lead exceeds about three scores in the fourth quarter) truncate attempts and, for protected contracts, determine voiding. A backup who appears late has a very short window. The model must separate the voided states from the realized-count distribution. nfl.qb is used for starter status only; its catalog QB point value estimated from market line moves is not used.
stages.distribution: Discrete states (does not play / plays full game / pulled early); pull probability rises steeply with lead size in Q4

stages.name: Pass attempt volume from script and pace
stages.description: Attempts equal team dropbacks (plays times pass rate) minus sacks and scrambles. Pass rate depends on expected game state: trailing teams pass much more; the team's neutral pass tendency (PROE), pace, weather (wind) and the run-game quality all shape the distribution. Attempts per game by QB are overdispersed and correlated with the score differential.
stages.distribution: Negative-binomial-like count with mean 28-40; strongly script-dependent; right-skewed

stages.name: Per-attempt TD probability and goal-line allocation
stages.description: Per-attempt TD probability is the sum of long completions (low probability, any field position) and short-yardage red-zone throws. The team's goal-to-go pass rate, the quality of red-zone targets (TE/WR availability), defensive red-zone performance and the QB's own rushing at the goal line determine how many team TDs are passes. TD luck regresses hard: a QB's season TD rate over expectation is mostly noise. Red-zone catcher quality (nfl.red_zone_target_quality) lifts or lowers the per-attempt TD rate for the same QB.
stages.distribution: Binomial thinning of attempts; heavy dependence on red-zone dropback count (about 4 to 6 per game); strong regression to expectation

stages.name: Interception generation process
stages.description: Interceptions arise from throws into coverage: turnover-worthy throw rate (decision quality), pressure, depth of target, ball-hawk defenders and randomness (tipped passes, receivers' bobbles). A single bad game is largely luck; QB-level rate regresses to mean with a half-life of many attempts. Defence-level interception propensity is mostly random but has a skill component (zone coverage with ball-hawk safeties, pass rush forcing hurried throws).
stages.distribution: Low-rate counts: mean 0.6 to 1.0 per game; zero-heavy; overdispersion from game script

stages.name: Dispersion, ladders and cross-statistic dependence
stages.description: TDs and INTs are not independent of attempts or of each other: trailing scripts increase attempts and both TDs and INTs; strong pass-rush games raise INTs and lower TDs. Rung probabilities P(>=k) must be monotone, and overdispersion widens the upper tail beyond Poisson, which is what 4+ TD and 2+ INT rungs depend on.
stages.distribution: Mixed Poisson (gamma-mixed) counts with positive correlation between TD and INT counts via attempts; discrete monotone ladder

stages.name: Career accumulation toward a milestone
stages.description: KXNFLCAREERPASSTDS (title only) is a career milestone: the probability of crossing a career total depends on the remaining distance, expected games per future season (injury attrition, benching, retirement hazard by age), the per-game TD rate with age decline and offensive-system changes, so it is a sum over a random number of remaining seasons and games rather than a per-game question. The single-season accrual series is no longer filed here.
stages.distribution: Sum of per-game counts over a random number of games across seasons; retirement and injury truncate; age-dependent mean

stages.name: Settlement rules
stages.description: The label is determined by the official stat sheet, the fair-price void for no live play, the half-time protected rule (no postponement clause appears in the sampled TD/INT texts); passing TD credit excludes plays nullified by penalty, and stat corrections can change counts.
stages.distribution: Deterministic rules plus small stat-correction probability

nfl.qb_expected_pass_td.label: QB expected passing TDs (xPassTD) from dropback-level location and target
nfl.qb_expected_pass_td.mechanism: Sum over a QB's dropbacks of the probability that the attempt becomes a TD given field position, down, distance, target type and defensive look.
nfl.qb_expected_pass_td.rationale: Realized TD counts are noisy; a location-based expectation separates opportunity from finishing luck and gives the per-attempt TD rate that actually predicts forward counts.
nfl.qb_expected_pass_td.measurement: Fit a logistic model P(pass TD | yardline_100, down, ydstogo, air_yards bucket, pass_location, offense_personnel, defenders_in_box) on 2006+ pass attempts using pbp-only fields (yardline_100, down, ydstogo, air_yards bucket, pass_location) and, as an upgrade fitted only on the participation era (about 2016+), offense_personnel and defenders_in_box, which are not available for earlier seasons; for each QB, expected TDs per attempt = average over his attempts last 700 attempts (half-life 350 attempts); shrink to team-level rate with k=300 attempts; ratio of actual to expected regressed 70% to 1.0; as-of previous game.

nfl.goal_to_go_pass_rate.label: Team goal-to-go and inside-20 pass rate by zone and down
nfl.goal_to_go_pass_rate.mechanism: Share of snaps that are dropbacks in the zones 20-11, 10-6, 5-1 yards, by down and score state, by team and coach.
nfl.goal_to_go_pass_rate.rationale: The share of team TDs that are passing depends on goal-to-go play-calling; it varies from about 30% to 70% across teams and drives the QB's TD count more than the total.
nfl.goal_to_go_pass_rate.measurement: From pbp 2 seasons (half-life 20 games): dropback rate in each zone by down and score_differential bucket; coach random effect shrunk with k=25 plays per zone; blend for new coordinator with league prior; output expected passing TDs fraction of team TDs given the team's red-zone trips; as-of previous game.
raw_data: pbp: yardline_100, down, play_type, pass_attempt, score_differential, posteam
nfl.goal_to_go_pass_rate.why: Controls pass versus run allocation of the team TD pool, the key factor between team total and QB TDs.

nfl.qb_attempt_forecast.label: QB pass-attempt count distribution by script and environment
nfl.qb_attempt_forecast.mechanism: Forecast distribution of the QB's attempts using team plays, pass rate conditional on expected state, sacks, wind and QB participation.
nfl.qb_attempt_forecast.rationale: Attempts are the exposure for TDs, completions and INTs; ignoring their conditional distribution across scripts mixes games where the QB throws 25 times and 45 times.
nfl.qb_attempt_forecast.measurement: Negative-binomial regression on 2015+ QB-games (starting QBs) of pass attempts on log expected team plays (nfl.total_plays_state_model), neutral PROE (nfl.proe), own-model expected margin bucket (<=-7, -7..-3, -3..3, 3..7, >7 from nfl.own_team_rating_market_free; never a betting spread), wind>=15 mph flag, dome flag, opponent rush-EPA-allowed rank, with team random effect; output mean and NB dispersion. Mix over P(QB pulled early) from nfl.qb_blowout_pull_threshold (attempts after exit set to 0). As-of start of week; refit each season, walk-forward.
raw_data: QB-game attempts, team plays, expected margin bucket, wind, dome, opponent run-defence rank
nfl.qb_attempt_forecast.why: Gives the opportunity count with its dispersion, rather than a mean pass rate.

nfl.qb_blowout_pull_hazard.label: QB blowout pull and early-exit hazard
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_hazard.mechanism: Probability that the QB leaves the game early because of a lopsided score or injury, as a function of lead and time.
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_hazard.rationale: Protected and standard contracts differ on pulls; a QB pulled up 28 in the fourth quarter has truncated counts and the protected contract voids.
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_hazard.measurement: From pbp 2010-2025: hazard that the starting QB's last snap occurs before game end, by lead size and clock; coach random effect (k=8 blowout games); combine with in-game injury hazard by QB mobility; P(plays 2H) and P(pulled with lead>=21 before end of Q3); as-of start of week.
raw_data: pbp: passer_id by play, score_differential, game_seconds_remaining
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_hazard.why: Quantifies the void and truncation states of the contract.

nfl.opp_def_int_propensity.label: Opponent defence interception propensity, QB-quality adjusted
nfl.opp_def_int_propensity.mechanism: Opponent's interceptions per attempt over expectation given the quality of QBs faced and pressure generated.
nfl.opp_def_int_propensity.rationale: Interception counts by defence are heavily luck; the skill component (ball skills, safety range) must be separated from the pressure effect and from opposing QB quality.
nfl.opp_def_int_propensity.measurement: Interceptions per attempt faced by the defence, adjusted by opposing QB turnover-worthy rate (season), pressure rate faced and pass depth; regress to league mean with k=350 attempts; recency half-life 12 games; as-of previous game.

nfl.qb_career_milestone_accrual.label: Season and career passing-TD accrual model with games and aging
nfl.qb_career_milestone_accrual.mechanism: Projected remaining TDs given per-game rate, games remaining, availability and aging curve.
nfl.qb_career_milestone_accrual.rationale: Season (40+) and career markets are sums over games; the distribution of games played and a QB's age-related change in TD rate matter as much as the per-game mean.
nfl.qb_career_milestone_accrual.measurement: Per-game TD mean from nfl.qb_expected_pass_td and attempt forecast, trend by age (QB aging curve estimated 2000-2025: attempts flat then decline from age 35, TD rate regressed), games remaining from schedule minus byes, availability from injury hazard (QB games missed per season by age and mobility, beta prior); simulate season totals with negative binomial game counts; as-of previous game.
